heading: Change a running swarm > When it fails
summary: Six ids belong to the three changes.
text:
Six ids belong to the three changes. Read the one your command printed.

- [`FLEET_RETIRE_REFUSED`](../../docs/troubleshooting.md#fleet_retire_refused) comes from `retire`, and from `replace`, when the swarm is not running, the agent is unknown, or the role would fall below its `min`. Check the names with `fleet queue`.
- [`FLEET_NOT_NOW`](../../docs/troubleshooting.md#fleet_not_now) appears when a control does not apply to the workload's present state, such as `done` on a swarm that is not running. The line lists the states it does apply to.
- [`FLEET_DONE_NEVER_STARTED`](../../docs/troubleshooting.md#fleet_done_never_started) shows that no agent of the swarm ever started, so there is no team to end. Run `fleet cancel ID` in its place.
- [`FLEET_PRUNE_REFUSED`](../../docs/troubleshooting.md#fleet_prune_refused) appears when `--merged` is not a full commit id, or when the workload is not a swarm that is done or cancelled.
- [`FLEET_NOT_FOUND`](../../docs/troubleshooting.md#fleet_not_found) shows that your role sees no such workload, since a workload of another project reads as unknown to you.
- [`FLEET_NOT_A_MEMBER`](../../docs/troubleshooting.md#fleet_not_a_member) answers a command for a project you do not belong to. An admin runs `org members add` for you.

heading: Rules for the agents in this repository
text:
<!--
Copy this file to the root of your repository as AGENTS.md. Delete the front matter, the line that starts with ">"
and this comment. Then fill in each part for your project. Claude Code and Codex read AGENTS.md when they start, and
so does every agent Dockingbird runs on your repository, after Dockingbird's own rules. To give one agent a different
file and leave your checkout as it is, start it with `dockingbird claude --agent-md FILE` (or `codex`, or `start`).
For each rule, say what the agent should do and which command shows that it did.
-->

heading: Rules for the agents in this repository > The project
summary: What this repository builds, who it is for, and where its documents are, in one short paragraph.
text: What this repository builds, who it is for, and where its documents are, in one short paragraph.

heading: Rules for the agents in this repository > Before you change anything
summary: - Read the documents the task names first, then the code it touches.
text:
- Read the documents the task names first, then the code it touches.
- Change only what the task asks for. Anything else you notice goes in your report, not in the code.
- Ask when the task is unclear instead of guessing: a question costs less than a wrong change.

heading: Rules for the agents in this repository > Build and test
summary: - Set up: the command that installs the project's dependencies.
text:
- Set up: the command that installs the project's dependencies.
- Test: the command that runs the tests, and how to run only the ones a change touches.
- Check: the formatter, the linter and the type checker, each with its command.

Write the failing test first, then the change, then run the tests again. A test stays as it is: change the code
until it passes, and never skip, weaken or delete a test to get there.

heading: Rules for the agents in this repository > Code
summary: - The style this repository follows, and where its guide is.
text:
- The style this repository follows, and where its guide is.
- Read secrets from the environment the project names, so none lands in code, logs, tests or commits.
- Keep each change small and each function about one thing.

heading: Rules for the agents in this repository > Commits
summary: - Commit once per finished step.
text:
- Commit once per finished step. The message says what changed and why.
- Add new commits on top of shared history. Do not force push or rebase a shared branch.
- Your work reaches the repository's owner only as commits, and the owner reviews every one.

heading: Rules for the agents in this repository > When you are done
summary: Say what you changed, what you ran to check it and what it printed, and what you could not check.
text:
Say what you changed, what you ran to check it and what it printed, and what you could not check. You are done when
every check named under "Build and test" has run on your change and its output is in your report.

heading: Install fails
summary: This page follows the install from the first command to the first `dockingbird claude` and names every place it can stop.
text: This page follows the install from the first command to the first `dockingbird claude` and names every place it can stop. Each step gives what the screen shows, the message id when Dockingbird printed it, and the fix. Ids link to the [catalogue](../troubleshooting.md). Steps 1 to 3 happen before Dockingbird exists on the computer, so uv prints them and they carry no id.

heading: Install fails > Before you start
summary: The install is done when uv exits 0 and this command prints a version.
text:
| You need | The check | If it is missing |
|---|---|---|
| An Apple silicon Mac or arm64 Linux | `uname -m` prints `arm64` on a Mac and `aarch64` on Linux | Use another computer |
| uv | `uv --version` prints a version | `brew install uv` on a Mac |
| git at `/usr/bin/git` | `/usr/bin/git --version` prints a version | Install git |
| Docker Desktop, or Docker Engine with buildx on Linux | `docker version` and `docker buildx version` print versions | Install Docker |
| Your license key | The purchase email holds it | See the support page |

The install is done when uv exits 0 and this command prints a version.

```bash
dockingbird --version
```

heading: Install fails > Step 1. A bare install
summary: The command `uv tool install dockingbird` with no index installs a package of that name from the public index.
text:
The command `uv tool install dockingbird` with no index installs a package of that name from the public index. That package is not Dockingbird. Nothing from Dockingbird prints, because the installed program is not ours.

Remove it, then run the full command from step 2.

```bash
uv tool uninstall dockingbird
```

heading: Install fails > Step 2. A key that is wrong or revoked
summary: The install command hands the key to uv as the index's password, through the environment.
text:
The install command hands the key to uv as the index's password, through the environment.

```bash
UV_INDEX_ZEUSFYI_USERNAME=license UV_INDEX_ZEUSFYI_PASSWORD="$(pbpaste)" uv tool install dockingbird --index zeusfyi=https://license.zeus.fyi/simple/
```

A wrong, truncated or revoked key makes the release index answer with an HTTP 401. uv reports the refusal and installs nothing. Dockingbird is not on the computer yet, so no message id exists for this failure.

The fix has three checks.

1. Copy the key from the purchase email again. The `pbpaste` in the command reads whatever is on the clipboard, so a link or a copied sentence in its place fails.
2. On Linux, run `read -rs UV_INDEX_ZEUSFYI_PASSWORD`, paste the key, press Enter, and use `"$UV_INDEX_ZEUSFYI_PASSWORD"` in place of `"$(pbpaste)"`. Run `unset UV_INDEX_ZEUSFYI_PASSWORD` when uv is done.
3. If the key is right and the 401 stays, the license may have ended. See [SUPPORT.md](../../SUPPORT.md) for where to ask.

heading: Install fails > Step 3. A trial
summary: The index serves an active license only, so a trial cannot install from it.
text: The index serves an active license only, so a trial cannot install from it. Install with a license key as in step 2, then run `dockingbird license activate`.

heading: Install fails > Step 4. The command is not found
summary: uv installed Dockingbird, but the shell does not know where uv puts programs.
text:
uv installed Dockingbird, but the shell does not know where uv puts programs. The shell prints its own "command not found".

```bash
uv tool update-shell
```

Open a new terminal, then run `dockingbird --version` again. The step is done when it prints a version.

heading: Install fails > Step 5. Tab completion run twice
summary: `dockingbird completion --install` adds tab completion.
text:
`dockingbird completion --install` adds tab completion. A second run is not a failure. It prints [COMPLETION_ALREADY](../troubleshooting.md#completion_already) and exits 0.

```text
Tab completion for {shell} was installed already; its script is current:
  {path}
  {rc} sources it
```

heading: Install fails > Step 6. Activation stops
summary: `dockingbird license activate` is the first command that reaches the license server.
text:
`dockingbird license activate` is the first command that reaches the license server. Three messages can stop it here.

- [LICENSE_KEY_IN_ARGV](../troubleshooting.md#license_key_in_argv) exits 2. You typed the key after the command. Nothing ran. Run `dockingbird license activate` alone and paste the key when asked.
- [LICENSE_KEY_INVALID](../troubleshooting.md#license_key_invalid) exits 1. The server does not know that key, or the text is not a key. Nothing changed. Copy the key again and rerun the command.
- [LICENSE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED](../troubleshooting.md#license_platform_unsupported) exits 1. This computer is an Intel Mac, an x86 Linux machine or Windows.

The platform message reads like this.

```text
Dockingbird's license program runs on Apple silicon Macs and arm64
Linux, not on {platform}.
```

No fix exists on that computer. Dockingbird runs on Apple silicon Macs and arm64 Linux only. Use one of those, or an arm64 cloud VM.

When the server cannot be reached, the command prints [LICENSE_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE](../troubleshooting.md#license_authority_unavailable) and changes nothing. Get online and run it again. The [licensing guide](../guides/licensing.md) lists the other license messages.

heading: Install fails > Step 7. Docker is missing
summary: The first `dockingbird claude` checks Docker before it builds anything.
text:
The first `dockingbird claude` checks Docker before it builds anything.

[DOCKER_NOT_INSTALLED](../troubleshooting.md#docker_not_installed) exits 1 when no `docker` command exists. On a Mac it prints this.

```text
Dockingbird needs Docker Desktop. Install it, then run this again:
  https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/
```

On Linux it names `https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/` instead. Install Docker, then run the command again.

[DOCKER_NOT_RUNNING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_not_running) exits 1 when Docker is installed but did not start in time. Start Docker Desktop and run the command again.

[DOCKER_BUILDX_MISSING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_buildx_missing) exits 1 when Docker has no buildx plugin. Docker Desktop includes it, so update Docker Desktop. On Linux, install Docker's `docker-buildx-plugin` package.

heading: Install fails > Step 8. git is missing
summary: The prerequisite is git at `/usr/bin/git`.
text: The prerequisite is git at `/usr/bin/git`. The catalogue holds no message for a missing git, so the check is yours: `/usr/bin/git --version` must print a version. Install git so that `/usr/bin/git` exists, then run `dockingbird claude` again.

heading: Install fails > When it fails
summary: The cookbook [recover from a failed install](../../examples/recover-from-a-failed-install/README.md) runs the three main failures with their fixes.
text:
| Message id | What it means and the fix |
|---|---|
| [COMPLETION_ALREADY](../troubleshooting.md#completion_already) | Informs only, exit 0. |
| [LICENSE_KEY_IN_ARGV](../troubleshooting.md#license_key_in_argv) | Paste the key when asked. |
| [LICENSE_KEY_INVALID](../troubleshooting.md#license_key_invalid) | Copy the key again. |
| [LICENSE_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED](../troubleshooting.md#license_platform_unsupported) | Use Apple silicon or arm64 Linux. |
| [LICENSE_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE](../troubleshooting.md#license_authority_unavailable) | Get online, then run it again. |
| [DOCKER_NOT_INSTALLED](../troubleshooting.md#docker_not_installed) | Install Docker. |
| [DOCKER_NOT_RUNNING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_not_running) | Start Docker. |
| [DOCKER_BUILDX_MISSING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_buildx_missing) | Install the buildx plugin. |

The cookbook [recover from a failed install](../../examples/recover-from-a-failed-install/README.md) runs the three main failures with their fixes. The next failure a reader meets is [the first start stops](first-start-stops.md), and the one after is [a license refused](licence-refused.md).

heading: License refused
summary: This page tells each license failure as a story.
text: This page tells each license failure as a story. The stories are a key that is not taken, seats that are full, a computer that was freed, a trial already used and a term that is over. Each part gives the message id, what the screen shows and the fix. The commands behind it are on the [licensing guide](../guides/licensing.md). A start refused for a license, `LICENSE_REFUSED`, is not yet available.

heading: License refused > Before you start
summary: - Dockingbird is installed.
text:
- Dockingbird is installed. Check with `dockingbird --version`.
- You know which license key this computer should use. It is in the purchase email.
- `dockingbird license status` runs. It reads the license file on this computer and works offline.

heading: License refused > 1. The key is not taken
summary: You run `dockingbird license activate` and paste the key.
text:
You run `dockingbird license activate` and paste the key. Two messages stop it before the server counts a seat.

[LICENSE_KEY_IN_ARGV](../troubleshooting.md#license_key_in_argv) exits 2 when the key follows the command on the line. Nothing ran. Run `dockingbird license activate` with no argument and paste the key when it asks.

[LICENSE_KEY_INVALID](../troubleshooting.md#license_key_invalid) exits 1 when the server does not know the key or the text is not a key. The key is never shown, so check what you pasted.

```text
{publisher} doesn't know that license key; nothing changed.
Check it, then: dockingbird license activate
```

Copy the key again from the purchase email and run the command again.

heading: License refused > 2. Seats are full
summary: The license admits its seats times three computers, and every one is linked.
text:
The license admits its seats times three computers, and every one is linked. The third computer of a one-seat license succeeds. A fourth one gets [LICENSE_SEATS_FULL](../troubleshooting.md#license_seats_full) and exit 1.

```text
Every computer this license admits is linked, so this one can't join.
Free one: dockingbird license activations --release ID
```

Under those lines the command names each linked computer, the one seen longest ago first, with its id. Pick the computer you no longer use and free it.

```bash
dockingbird license activations --release ID
```

The fix worked when the product prints [LICENSE_ACTIVATION_RELEASED](../troubleshooting.md#license_activation_released) and lists the rest.

```text
The seat of activation {id} is free again.
```

Run `dockingbird license activate` again on this computer. It prints `This computer is activated:` and the count of linked computers. The [seat cookbook](../../examples/move-your-seat/README.md) walks the same fix with a new laptop.

heading: License refused > 3. A computer that was freed
summary: Say you freed the seat of your old laptop from your new one.
text:
Say you freed the seat of your old laptop from your new one. The old laptop still has its license file until it checks in. When it runs `dockingbird license status --refresh`, the screen shows the state under [LICENSE_SHOWN](../troubleshooting.md#license_shown) and exits 0.

```text
This computer's seat was freed from another computer.
Activate it again: dockingbird license activate
```

Run `dockingbird license activate` on that laptop only if you want it back on the license. If the other computers hold every link by then, that command meets step 2 and `LICENSE_SEATS_FULL`.

Two other status lines have the same fix. `The license file here is another computer's.` appears when the file came from a different computer, and its next step is `Activate this one: dockingbird license activate`. `The license file here can't be read.` appears when the file is damaged, and its next step is `Activate it again: dockingbird license activate`.

heading: License refused > 4. A trial already used
summary: A trial starts with `dockingbird license trial`.
text:
A trial starts with `dockingbird license trial`. It is allowed once per computer.

```text
This computer has had its trial already.
Activate it with a key: dockingbird license activate
```

That is [LICENSE_TRIAL_USED](../troubleshooting.md#license_trial_used), exit 1. Activate with a key. A trial cannot install from the release index and cannot update. An index install on a trial computer meets [LICENSE_UPDATE_NEEDS_LICENSE](../troubleshooting.md#license_update_needs_license) at `dockingbird update`. It exits 1 and changes nothing.

```text
Updating Dockingbird needs this computer's license: its release index
lets in only an activated computer. Nothing changed.
Activate it: dockingbird license activate
```

heading: License refused > 5. The term is over
summary: The term is the period the license names.
text:
The term is the period the license names. Before it ends, an agent start prints one line from [LICENSE_NOTE](../troubleshooting.md#license_note) and the agent starts.

```text
Your Dockingbird license ends {until}; renew it to keep starting new agents.
```

After it ends, `dockingbird license status` prints this.

```text
The license's term ended.
Renew it, then: dockingbird license status --refresh
```

The installed version keeps working. New releases need a renewed license. Renew, then run `dockingbird license status --refresh` to read the new term. The grace period after a term ends is the length the license names.

heading: License refused > 6. The server or the license program is out of reach
summary: [LICENSE_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE](../troubleshooting.md#license_authority_unavailable) exits 1 when the license server cannot be reached.
text:
[LICENSE_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE](../troubleshooting.md#license_authority_unavailable) exits 1 when the license server cannot be reached. Nothing changed. Get online and run the command again. An offline `status` without `--refresh` still works.

```text
Dockingbird couldn't reach the license server, so nothing changed.
Try again later.
```

The license program is a small file Dockingbird downloads on the first `dockingbird license` command. Three ids mean it is missing or damaged, and each prints its fix.

- [LICENSE_CLIENT_UNAVAILABLE](../troubleshooting.md#license_client_unavailable): the download failed. Run `dockingbird license status`, which downloads it again.
- [LICENSE_CLIENT_DAMAGED](../troubleshooting.md#license_client_damaged): the program did not answer as expected. Run `dockingbird update`.
- [LICENSE_CLIENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH](../troubleshooting.md#license_client_digest_mismatch): the download is not the one this version expects, so it was not kept. Run `dockingbird update`.

heading: First start stops
summary: This page follows `cd your-repo && dockingbird claude` from its first check to the running agent.
text: This page follows `cd your-repo && dockingbird claude` from its first check to the running agent. Each step names the message id, what the screen shows and the fix. Ids link to the [catalogue](../troubleshooting.md).

heading: First start stops > Before you start
summary: - Dockingbird is installed and `dockingbird --version` prints a version.
text:
- Dockingbird is installed and `dockingbird --version` prints a version.
- You are in a git checkout of your project. Check with `git status`.
- Docker answers. Check with `docker version`.
- The first run builds the image once. Expect about 5 minutes and about 1 GB of downloads.

The start is done when the screen prints these two lines, with your repo and branch.

```text
Starting claude-1 on myapp (main).
To leave it working, close this window.
```

heading: First start stops > Step 1. A file in the home
summary: Dockingbird keeps its files in `~/.local/share/dockingbird`, or in the folder `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME` names.
text:
Dockingbird keeps its files in `~/.local/share/dockingbird`, or in the folder `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME` names. It refuses a folder that holds files it did not make. This is [HOME_NOT_EMPTY](../troubleshooting.md#home_not_empty), exit 1, and nothing is set up.

```text
{folder} already has files Dockingbird didn't make, so it won't use it.
In it: {names:and}.
Move those files out of it (your own rules can stay in instructions/),
or set DOCKINGBIRD_HOME to an empty or new folder, then run this again.
```

Some names do not count: `instructions`, `vaults`, `versions.toml`, `config.toml`, `browser-solver.json`, `hosts.toml`, `fleet.toml`, Finder's `.DS_Store` file and an empty `logs` folder. Move the listed files out, or point `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME` at an absolute path that does not exist yet. Avoid a space or any of `%$"'\` in that path.

A variant says the folder is your home folder or one above it. Dockingbird never uses those, so choose another path.

heading: First start stops > Step 2. A folder that is not a checkout
summary: The command works on a repo.
text:
The command works on a repo. In any other folder it stops with [NOT_A_GIT_REPO](../troubleshooting.md#not_a_git_repo) and exit 1.

```text
Not a git repo: {path}.
cd into your project, then run this again.
```

Two relatives stop the same way. [SUBMODULE_NOT_YET](../troubleshooting.md#submodule_not_yet) appears inside a submodule, and [WORKTREE_NOT_YET](../troubleshooting.md#worktree_not_yet) appears in a git worktree. Both ask you to `cd` into the repository's main checkout and run the command again.

The command `dockingbird init` has its own pair. [INIT_NOT_A_CHECKOUT](../troubleshooting.md#init_not_a_checkout) says `{path} is not in a git repo, so there is nothing to set up.` and [INIT_INSIDE_HOME](../troubleshooting.md#init_inside_home) says the same for a folder inside the Dockingbird home. Run `dockingbird init` in your repo.

heading: First start stops > Step 3. Files the agents do not take
summary: Before it sets anything up, Dockingbird checks the branch.
text:
Before it sets anything up, Dockingbird checks the branch. A symlink that leaves the repo, a submodule or a Git LFS file is refused within seconds. This is [LINK_TREE_POLICY](../troubleshooting.md#link_tree_policy), exit 1.

```text
{repo} ({branch}) can't be linked yet: it has {count} files the agents don't take:
{entries}
Fix them, commit, then run this again.
```

Each entry names its kind, and a symlink shows where it points. A relative symlink that stays inside the repo is fine. Remove or replace each listed file, commit, and run the command again.

heading: First start stops > Step 4. Docker is not ready
summary: Dockingbird starts Docker Desktop when it is off.
text:
Dockingbird starts Docker Desktop when it is off. [DOCKER_STARTING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_starting) and [DOCKER_WAKING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_waking) only inform and exit 0. They end with the seconds it took.

```text
Waking Docker ... ready ({elapsed})
```

When Docker does not come up, one of these stops the start, each with exit 1.

| Message id | What it means and the fix |
|---|---|
| [DOCKER_NOT_RUNNING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_not_running) | Start Docker Desktop, then run the command again. |
| [DOCKER_NOT_ANSWERING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_not_answering) | Docker took a request and never answered. Restart Docker Desktop. |
| [DOCKER_ANSWERING_SLOWLY](../troubleshooting.md#docker_answering_slowly) | Docker answers too late, as on a busy Mac. Check Docker Desktop. |
| [HOME_NOT_SHARED](../troubleshooting.md#home_not_shared) | Docker Desktop does not share the folder. Add it under Settings, Resources, File sharing. |
| [DOCKER_BUILDX_MISSING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_buildx_missing) | Update Docker Desktop, or install `docker-buildx-plugin` on Linux. |

heading: First start stops > Step 5. The build
summary: The build takes about 5 minutes and shows a progress line.
text:
The build takes about 5 minutes and shows a progress line. Ctrl-C ends it with [SETUP_INTERRUPTED](../troubleshooting.md#setup_interrupted), exit 1.

```text
Set-up didn't finish. Nothing changed. Run this again.
```

Run the command again. A failed step stops with [IMAGE_BUILD_FAILED](../troubleshooting.md#image_build_failed) and exit 1. It names the step.

```bash
dockingbird --verbose claude
```

The `--verbose` flag shows Docker's own output for that step. [HOME_SETUP_TOOK_TOO_LONG](../troubleshooting.md#home_setup_took_too_long) means a tool's home took longer than Dockingbird waits, usually because the computer was busy. Run the command again when the load drops.

heading: First start stops > Step 6. The copy of your branch
summary: The start copies your branch for the agents.
text:
The start copies your branch for the agents. It is done when the line ends with the size and the time.

```text
Copying myapp (main) for the agents ({size}) ... done ({elapsed})
```

[REPO_LINKING](../troubleshooting.md#repo_linking) is that line and only informs. [REPO_DISK_FULL](../troubleshooting.md#repo_disk_full) exits 1 when Docker's virtual disk has too little room for the history. Free space in Docker Desktop, under Settings and Resources, or run `docker system prune`, then run the command again.

heading: First start stops > Step 7. A sign-in that never finishes
summary: The first start of a tool signs in once, inside the container.
text:
The first start of a tool signs in once, inside the container. The start line says what will happen.

```text
Starting claude-1 on myapp (main). Claude will show a sign-in link:
open it on this Mac, sign in, then paste the code here. Only this once.
```

Open the link on the Mac, sign in, and paste the code back. That line is [SIGNIN_FIRST_TIME](../troubleshooting.md#signin_first_time). Codex shows a code and a link instead, and you enter the code on the page. If its device sign-in is off, turn it on in ChatGPT's security settings.

When you quit the sign-in, or never use the link, the agent ends with [SIGNIN_NEEDED](../troubleshooting.md#signin_needed) and exit 1. Its empty copy is removed.

```text
Claude isn't signed in yet. Run dockingbird claude again to sign in.
Or use an API key: dockingbird login claude --api-key
```

Run `dockingbird claude` again, or sign in on its own.

```bash
dockingbird login claude
```

The sign-in worked when the product prints [SIGNIN_DONE](../troubleshooting.md#signin_done).

```text
Claude is signed in.
```

[SIGNIN_FAILED](../troubleshooting.md#signin_failed) exits 1 when the screen did not finish, and nothing changed. [SIGNIN_NOT_SAVED](../troubleshooting.md#signin_not_saved) exits 1 when it finished but could not be kept. Run `dockingbird login claude` again for either. With no Claude or ChatGPT account, use an API key with `dockingbird login claude --api-key` or `dockingbird login codex --api-key`.

heading: First start stops > When it fails
summary: The page before this one is [a license refused](licence-refused.md).
text:
| Message id | What it means and the fix |
|---|---|
| [HOME_NOT_EMPTY](../troubleshooting.md#home_not_empty) | Move the files out or set `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME`. |
| [NOT_A_GIT_REPO](../troubleshooting.md#not_a_git_repo) | `cd` into your project. |
| [INIT_NOT_A_CHECKOUT](../troubleshooting.md#init_not_a_checkout) | Run `dockingbird init` in your repo. |
| [LINK_TREE_POLICY](../troubleshooting.md#link_tree_policy) | Fix the listed files and commit. |
| [DOCKER_NOT_RUNNING](../troubleshooting.md#docker_not_running) | Start Docker. |
| [SETUP_INTERRUPTED](../troubleshooting.md#setup_interrupted) | Run the command again. |
| [IMAGE_BUILD_FAILED](../troubleshooting.md#image_build_failed) | Run again with `--verbose`. |
| [REPO_DISK_FULL](../troubleshooting.md#repo_disk_full) | Free Docker's disk. |
| [SIGNIN_NEEDED](../troubleshooting.md#signin_needed) | Sign in, or use an API key. |
| [SIGNIN_FAILED](../troubleshooting.md#signin_failed) | Run `dockingbird login claude` again. |

heading: Troubleshooting
summary: Find your message: search this page for a few of its words, leaving out
text:
Find your message: search this page for a few of its words, leaving out
names, numbers and paths, which show here as values in braces. Each entry
says when the message appears, what it says, the next step it gives and its
exit status. A value in braces, such as `{repo}`, is filled in when the
message prints: `{name}` is an agent's name, `{tool}` is claude or codex
and `{harness}` Claude or Codex, `{subcommand}` is the command that picks
an agent up as it ran (its config's command, such as notes, with
--terminal for one that ran at a terminal; else claude or codex, or start
for one that worked without a terminal) and `{config_command}` that
config's command alone, `{repo}` and `{branch}` are your repo and branch,
and `{checkout}` is its folder; `{count:commit|commits}` is a number with
its noun, a list such as `{names:and}` is filled in with its entries, and
`{names:first}` with the first one. The messages are grouped by what you
were doing.

With `--verbose`, every message also shows its ID, which is its heading here.
With `--json`, each message is one line of JSON with the same exit status.

Exit statuses: 0 done, 1 a problem Dockingbird printed (with its next step),
2 usage. `dockingbird claude` and `dockingbird codex` exit with the tool's own
status once it has started. The native commands (`dockingbird native ...`)
have their own messages and exit codes, in the
[operator guide](operator-guide.md).

heading: Install, Docker, licensing and the command line > UNKNOWN_COMMAND
summary: You typed a word where a command goes, and it isn't one of Dockingbird's commands.
text:
When: You typed a word where a command goes, and it isn't one of Dockingbird's commands. When it is close to one, the message suggests it. When the word is the removed command of an agent you named with `--as`, Dockingbird says instead that the agent waits until a config gives the command again.

```text
dockingbird: '{word}' is not a command.
See: dockingbird -h
```

Or:

```text
dockingbird: '{word}' is not a command. Did you mean '{suggestion}'?
See: dockingbird -h
```

Next step: dockingbird -h

Exit status: 2 (usage).

Dockingbird stops rather than ignore it. Test switches and the names Dockingbird's own commands read pass.

```text
Unset it, or fix its spelling, then run this again.
```

heading: Install, Docker, licensing and the command line > SETTING_REFUSED
summary: A setting in your shell (a variable with Dockingbird's prefix) can't be given to Dockingbird's containers as it stands, so the command stops before it runs rather than ignore it: its value isn't a whole number within the setting's range, two or more values break a rule between settings, its name is spelled in another case than upper case, or it is a setting of Dockingbird outside Docker (the database's address and roles, the developer's role switch and the host git's path), which Docker mode never uses.
text:
When: A setting in your shell (a variable with Dockingbird's prefix) can't be given to Dockingbird's containers as it stands, so the command stops before it runs rather than ignore it: its value isn't a whole number within the setting's range, two or more values break a rule between settings, its name is spelled in another case than upper case, or it is a setting of Dockingbird outside Docker (the database's address and roles, the developer's role switch and the host git's path), which Docker mode never uses.

```text
{names} must be a whole number from {low} to {high}.
Set a value in that range, or unset the variable, then run this again.
```

Or:

```text
{names} must be a whole number of {low} or more.
Set a value of at least that, or unset the variable, then run this again.
```

Or:

```text

Set each a value in its range, or unset the variables, then run this again.
```

Or:

```text
{names:and} would break a rule between Dockingbird's settings as they are set now.
Change or unset the settings named, then run this again.
```

Or:

```text
Dockingbird would not read {names:and}: a setting's name is spelled in upper case.
Spell each name in upper case, then run this again.
```

Or:

```text
Docker mode has no use for {names:and}: the value would be ignored.
Unset each variable named, then run this again.
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- Set a value in that range, or unset the variable, then run this again.
- Set a value of at least that, or unset the variable, then run this again.
- Set each a value in its range, or unset the variables, then run this again.
- Change or unset the settings named, then run this again.
- Spell each name in upper case, then run this again.
- Unset each variable named, then run this again.

Exit status: 2 (usage).

heading: Updates > UPDATE_UV_FAILED
summary: Installing the new Dockingbird with uv failed.
text:
When: Installing the new Dockingbird with uv failed. Each release goes into a folder of its own, and the message shows the exact command that installs it there, so you can run it yourself and see why; nothing else changed. For an install from the release index the command ran with this computer's download token, so check the network and `dockingbird license status` instead. When uv installed something other than the release, Dockingbird removed it again and says so: run `dockingbird update` once more.

```text
Getting the latest Dockingbird didn't work. Dockingbird ran:
  env \
    UV_TOOL_DIR={tool_dir} \
    UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR={bin_dir} \
    uv tool install --force --python 3.12 --from \
    git+{source_url} dockingbird
Run it yourself to see why. Nothing else changed.
```

Or:

```text
Getting the latest Dockingbird didn't work. Dockingbird ran:
  env \
    UV_TOOL_DIR={tool_dir} \
    UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR={bin_dir} \
    uv tool install --force --python 3.12 --from \
    git+{source_url}@{release} dockingbird
Run it yourself to see why. Nothing else changed.
```

Or:

```text
Getting the latest Dockingbird didn't work. Dockingbird ran:
  env \
    UV_TOOL_DIR={tool_dir} \
    UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR={bin_dir} \
    uv tool install --force --python 3.12 --from \
    git+{source_url}@{branch} dockingbird
Run it yourself to see why. Nothing else changed.
```

Or:

```text
Getting the latest Dockingbird didn't work. Dockingbird ran:
  env \
    UV_TOOL_DIR={tool_dir} \
    UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR={bin_dir} \
    uv tool install --force --python 3.12 --index \
    {license_index_name}={index_url} dockingbird=={version}
with this computer's download token for the release index.
Check the network and dockingbird license status, then run dockingbird update again. Nothing else changed.
```

Or:

```text
uv installed something other than Dockingbird {version}, so it was removed.
The command was:
  {uv_command}
Run it again: dockingbird update
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- Run it yourself to see why.
- dockingbird license status
- dockingbird update

heading: Homes, checkouts and toolchains > TRUST_NOTE
summary: The first attached start of a tool on a repo (`dockingbird claude` or `codex`, or `start --terminal`) where the repo's own settings are off: a repo that isn't trusted on this Mac (one you marked with `dockingbird trust --off`, or one with no mark while `config.toml` in Dockingbird's folder says `trust = "untrusted"`), a command whose config leaves them off, or a tool whose sign-in isn't yet proven safe from them.
text:
When: The first attached start of a tool on a repo (`dockingbird claude` or `codex`, or `start --terminal`) where the repo's own settings are off: a repo that isn't trusted on this Mac (one you marked with `dockingbird trust --off`, or one with no mark while `config.toml` in Dockingbird's folder says `trust = "untrusted"`), a command whose config leaves them off, or a tool whose sign-in isn't yet proven safe from them. Every other repo is trusted, and where its settings load neither tool asks, so nothing prints. With or without a terminal; a `start` on the bus prints none, nor does an agent in a scratch folder, where neither tool asks about the folder, so its start prints no note and waits for nothing. Claude may ask whether to trust its folder, and Codex, in a repo that isn't trusted, shows its folder-access notice each time it opens its screen (one Enter opens the folder restricted; a one-shot `codex exec` shows none); that folder is the agent's own copy. text:
When: You gave `--as` with arguments for the tool, with `--egress`, or with `--new`, for an agent that is already running. A running agent can't take new arguments or another egress, and `--new` can't take its name; you can reconnect to it or stop it, and with `--new` start a new agent under a name of its own. With `dockingbird start --as`, the agent runs already, so the message says how to send it a task instead. `dockingbird claude --as NAME` (or `codex`) of an agent that works on the bus, or whose container is gone, says the same: there is no terminal to reconnect to. Dockingbird itself refuses to start a second agent under a name that is running, so the same words come back when an agent started between the check and the start. The still-starting form: another command is starting the agent right now; a task you send reaches it once it runs. When that command starts it at a terminal (Codex waiting there for Enter before it opens, say), the message says to use it in that terminal instead: a terminal agent reads a task when you type in it. The form that asks you to run the command again: another command is starting an agent with no name yet, which may be this one, and is still making its copy, which takes minutes for a big repository's first agent.


```text
Use its terminal, or stop it: dockingbird stop {name}
```

It says so once, in the message's own thread, with how long the message has waited and which of these keeps it waiting, and the message goes in once that is over: the typing sent, the tool at its prompt and done, its screen still. Typing left unsent is cleared by Dockingbird once that has been said and no key has come for five minutes, which it says once more; a box taller than the screen, or a menu left open, can keep text the clear does not reach, and the message's turn is then told as failed. When the screen took bytes, the line says what kind, when, how many bytes that read had and the bytes that decided it in hex, so a key can be told from a terminal's answer.

```text

Someone is typing in its screen.
```

```text
This message had waited {elapsed}.
```

```text

```

Whatever the agent had already sent or done for the message stands.

If you deleted that branch, the message says `({branch}, no longer in your checkout)` where the forms below say `({branch})`, and its step makes the branch again first: `git switch -c {branch} dockingbird/{branch}` where they say `git switch {branch}`, or `git switch -c {branch}` when the agents' ref is gone too. The last form below shows one.

```text
{name} was stopped by the restart. Its copy is kept and may hold work:
dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
{name} was stopped by the restart. Its copy is kept in {repo} ({branch}) and may hold work.
To pick it up: git switch {branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
{name} was stopped by the restart. Its copy is kept in {repo} ({branch}) and may hold work.
To pick it up: cd {checkout}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
{name} was stopped by the restart. Its copy is kept in {repo} ({branch}) and may hold work.
To pick it up: cd {checkout}, then git switch {branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or, if you deleted that branch:

```text
{name} was stopped by the restart. Its copy is kept in {repo} ({branch}, no longer in your checkout) and may hold work.
To pick it up: git switch -c {branch} dockingbird/{branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
- git switch {branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
- cd {checkout}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
- cd {checkout}, then git switch {branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}

Exit status: 0 (done).

text:
When: You said yes to sync's merge (or a start's), and git stopped: before it merged anything, for example because your git has no name and email set (`git config --global user.name` and `user.email`), or after it started a merge it could not finish. A started merge that changed none of your files is cleared for you (or the message gives `git merge --quit` to clear it); one that changed your files is left as it is, to commit or to undo with `git merge --abort`. The message shows git's status and its last lines; fix what they say and run the command again.

```text
git merge stopped with status {status} before it began. Its last lines:
{entries}
Fix what git says, then run this again.
```

Or:

```text
git merge stopped with status {status} before it began and said nothing.
Run this again.
```

Or:

```text
git merge stopped with status {status} before it changed your files;
Dockingbird cleared the merge it had started. Its last lines:
{entries}
Fix what git says, then run this again.
```

Or:

```text
git merge stopped with status {status} before it changed your files,
and Dockingbird couldn't clear the merge it had started. Its last lines:
{entries}
When no other git runs here: git merge --quit, then run this again.
```

Or:

```text
git merge stopped with status {status} after it changed your files,
and the merge is still in progress. Its last lines:
{entries}
Fix what git says, then commit the merge (git commit), or undo it
(git merge --abort).
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- Fix what git says, then run this again.
- Run this again.
- git merge --quit, then run this again.
- Fix what git says, then commit the merge (git commit), or undo it (git merge --abort).

Exit status: 1 (a problem Dockingbird printed).

When: You ran `dockingbird logout`: the tool's sign-in and any saved key are gone. When Dockingbird followed this computer's own login of the tool, it stops following it; the login on this computer is unchanged, and `dockingbird login claude --here` (or `codex`) uses it again.

```text
Signed out of {harness}. Dockingbird has no {harness} sign-in or key now.
```

Or:

```text
Dockingbird stopped following this computer's {harness} login
and has no {harness} sign-in or key now.
Your own {harness} login here is unchanged. To use it again:
dockingbird login {tool} --here
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- none, where the message only informs
- dockingbird login {tool} --here

Exit status: 0 (done).

heading: Agents, status, sync and clean > STATUS_FAILED_NOTE
summary: Under "Needs your attention": a running agent's last turn failed, for example because Claude or Codex refused the request (an access or billing problem on the tool's side), with the tool's own error line when it gave one.
text:
When: Under "Needs your attention": a running agent's last turn failed, for example because Claude or Codex refused the request (an access or billing problem on the tool's side), with the tool's own error line when it gave one. The agent stays up but did nothing with that message. Fix the cause the error names, then send it the work again with the `dockingbird send` shown: a failed turn leaves the agent running, its next message starts a new turn in the same conversation, and it keeps the files it is working on and its jobs. A newer login reaches the agent between turns. If that turn fails too, stop the agent and pick it up with the command shown, which resumes its conversation but lets go of the files it was working on and its jobs. An agent that signs in with a saved Claude token (`dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -`) whose token stopped working (revoked or expired) keeps that token until it stops, so a send fails the same way: the note then says to make a new token with `claude setup-token`, stop the agent (Dockingbird saves a token only while no Claude agent runs), save the token and pick the agent up, which starts it on the new token. When that token is the one Claude Code uses on this computer, which Dockingbird follows, the note says to renew that login here instead, then stop and pick up the agent. The note names why the turn failed in one word, such as `server` or `auth`, when the agent says it.

```text
{name}'s last turn failed: {error}.
Recover it: dockingbird send {name} TEXT
It keeps what it works on and its jobs. If it fails again:
dockingbird stop {name}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

text:
When: A running agent whose last turn ended because Anthropic refused its sign-in, while Dockingbird tries that turn again by itself: a few times, a little longer apart each time, so a sign-in that changed meanwhile can reach the agent. For an agent on the message bus: the `dockingbird send` that gives it work, since it has no terminal to reconnect to. For an agent whose last turn failed: the recovery, a `dockingbird send`, which keeps the files it is working on and its jobs, or else stop it, then pick it up, which resumes its conversation; for one whose saved Claude token stopped working, a new token (`claude setup-token`), the stop, the token saved (`dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -`) and the pick-up, or, for a token Dockingbird follows from Claude Code on this computer, renewing that login here, then the stop and pick-up.

If you deleted that branch, its step makes the branch again first: `git switch -c {branch} dockingbird/{branch}` where the forms below say `git switch {branch}`, or `git switch -c {branch}` when the agents' ref is gone too. The last form below shows one.


Or:

```text
  pick it up   cd {checkout}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
  pick it up   cd {checkout}, then git switch {branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
  on the bus   dockingbird send {name} TEXT
```

Or:

```text
  its screen   send it a task: dockingbird send {name} TEXT, or see it: dockingbird {tool} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
  recover   dockingbird send {name} TEXT, or dockingbird stop {name}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
  recover   claude setup-token, then dockingbird stop {name}, then pbpaste | dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
  recover   renew Claude's login here, then dockingbird stop {name}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or, if you deleted that branch:

```text
  pick it up   git switch -c {branch} dockingbird/{branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- dockingbird {tool} --as {name}
- dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
- git switch {branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
- cd {checkout}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
- cd {checkout}, then git switch {branch}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
- dockingbird send {name} TEXT
- claude setup-token
- dockingbird stop {name}, then dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}

Exit status: 0 (done).

heading: Agents, status, sync and clean > STATUS_VERSIONS_DIFFER
summary: `status` while Dockingbird of another version runs with no agent in it.
text:
When: `status` while Dockingbird of another version runs with no agent in it. A `dockingbird` older than it lists the work kept as it last knew it, and its other commands stop until you update it; with a newer one, any other command finishes the update. When `dockingbird update` staged the newer one, it says Dockingbird switches by itself now and no command is needed, or, when that switch failed, that `dockingbird update` tries again. When that update waits for the agents to end, it names both versions, and the next line names the agents it waits for, or says the new version is taking over now when none is left. When the version of the Dockingbird running here can't be read, it says so and how to replace it: `dockingbird stop`, then `dockingbird update`.

```text
Dockingbird {running} is running, and this dockingbird is the older {version}.
This one shows the work kept as it last knew it, which can be out of date.
Use the newer one, or update this one: dockingbird update
```

Or:

```text
Dockingbird {running} is running, and this dockingbird is the newer {version}.
Any other command finishes the update, for example: dockingbird sync
```

Or:

```text
Dockingbird {running} is running, and this dockingbird is the newer {version}.
Dockingbird switches to {version} by itself now; no command is needed.
```

Or:

```text
Dockingbird {running} is running, and this dockingbird is the newer {version}.
The switch to {version} didn't work. See why and try again: dockingbird update
```

Or:

```text
Dockingbird {running} is running, and this dockingbird is the newer {version}.
```

Or:

```text
Dockingbird is running here, but its version can't be read,
and this dockingbird is {version}.
Replace it: dockingbird stop, then dockingbird update
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- dockingbird update
- dockingbird sync
- none, where the message only informs
- dockingbird stop

Exit status: 0 (done).

```text
claude mcp remove --scope user dockingbird, or codex mcp remove dockingbird
```

text:
When: `dockingbird connect` could not accept the reviewed JSON catalog. When it names the catalog file's path, the file itself was refused: it is missing, not a plain file of your own that only you can read, or reached through a link (on a Mac, `/tmp` is `/private/tmp`); give its real path. When the message names a field of the catalog (a remote, a branch or a port, say), that field is the one to fix; the message never shows what it says. For a key file, a `known_hosts` file, an API resource's `env_file`, or a provider's `adc_file`, `config_dir` or `config_file`, the catalog must give the real, absolute path of a file (for `config_dir`, a folder) of your own: not a relative path, one with `..` in it, or a link. When it says the catalog, or an entry of its resources or of a resource's projection, has a key Dockingbird doesn't know, a key of that JSON object (for a resource, its configuration too) is misspelled or doesn't belong there; the message never shows it.

```text

Review the JSON catalog before connecting.
```

Or:

```text

of your own that only you can read, with no link in its path.
Give its real path (on a Mac, /tmp is /private/tmp), then run this again.
```

```text
Fix it in the JSON catalog, then run this again.

```

Or:

```text

Fix it in the JSON catalog, then run this again.
```

- Give its real path (on a Mac, /tmp is /private/tmp), then run this again.
- Fix it in the JSON catalog, then run this again.

text:
When: You started an agent, or ran `dockingbird -h` or `dockingbird config list` in a repo, and `config.toml` in Dockingbird's folder can't be read as written: its `trust` line, which sets whether a repo you haven't marked is trusted, is something other than `"trusted"` or `"untrusted"`, or the file isn't TOML, or it isn't a plain file of yours Dockingbird can read (a link, which Dockingbird never follows there, a folder, a file too large or not UTF-8). Dockingbird never guesses which you meant: the start stops before anything runs, and the help and the list say it and go on without this repo's own configs. Fix the line or the file, or remove it: with no `trust` line, every repo is trusted unless you marked it with `dockingbird trust --off`, and `dockingbird trust` marks one trusted whatever the line says.

```text
{path}: trust must be "trusted" or "untrusted".
No agent starts until it is fixed.
Fix the line, or remove it: then every repo is trusted unless you mark it.
```

Or:

```text
{path} isn't TOML, so Dockingbird can't read its trust line,
trust = "trusted" or trust = "untrusted".
No agent starts until it is fixed.
Fix the file, or move it aside: then every repo is trusted unless you mark it.
```

Or:

```text
{path} isn't a regular file of yours, or is too large or not UTF-8,
so Dockingbird can't read its trust line.
No agent starts until it is fixed.
Make it a plain file of yours (a link won't do), or move it aside.
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- Fix the line, or remove it: then every repo is trusted unless you mark it.
- Fix the file, or move it aside: then every repo is trusted unless you mark it.
- Make it a plain file of yours (a link won't do), or move it aside.

```text
reach (its proxy admits no address of this computer), so nothing was started.
```

```text
{name} picks up where it left off, as a {config_command} agent at this terminal.
```

heading: Agents, status, sync and clean > START_COPY_FAILED
summary: You started an agent, and Dockingbird couldn't make the agents' copy of your branch for it, so nothing was started.
text:
When: You started an agent, and Dockingbird couldn't make the agents' copy of your branch for it, so nothing was started. The line says why, in one of these words: `the clone of the agents' copy failed or ran out of time`, `its folder in Dockingbird couldn't be made`, `its kept copy couldn't be resumed`, or `Dockingbird no longer lists this repo for it`; and it gives the command that starts it again, with `--as` and the agent's name when you named the agent, so the same agent starts. With `--verbose` it also names the error's code and reason and, for a clone, whether it ran out of time or how git ended; Dockingbird's log, `dockingbird.log` in its `logs` folder, keeps the same words. `dockingbird status` shows it under "Needs your attention" until a start on that branch gets going.

```text
{name}'s copy of {repo} ({branch}) couldn't be made: {why}.
Try again: dockingbird {subcommand}
```

Or:

```text
{name}'s copy of {repo} ({branch}) couldn't be made: {why}.
Try again: dockingbird {subcommand} --as {agent}
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- dockingbird {subcommand}
- dockingbird {subcommand} --as {agent}

heading: Install, Docker, licensing and the command line > NATIVE_REFUSED
summary: Dockingbird refused a message, inbox, artifact or results request, or a start or its task, and the line names its code and reason, and the field it refused when it names one.
text:
When: Dockingbird refused a message, inbox, artifact or results request, or a start or its task, and the line names its code and reason, and the field it refused when it names one. Check `dockingbird status` and the names, ids and text you gave. The payload forms: `dockingbird send --kind KIND` with a `--payload` (or none) that lacks a key the kind requires, has a key the kind does not take, or has a value the kind refuses; a review result's finding that is not minor needs its fix, what the fix changes (a rule, a file, a schema, a config key, a test or the product, and where), so a fix that is only a message is refused at that finding; nothing was sent, the line names the field and the keys, and the step is the same send with the kind's example payload. An unexpected error with a system error behind it names that error instead of a reason, for example `EIO`; `ENOSPC` means the agents' disk (Docker's) is full: free some of Docker's disk, or give it more (in Docker Desktop: Settings, Resources), then run it again.

```text
Dockingbird refused it: {code} ({reason}).
See: dockingbird status
```


```text

```


heading: The bus > SENT
summary: You ran `dockingbird send` and the message went; the line shows its id.
text:
When: You ran `dockingbird send` and the message went; the line shows its id. The ended form: the agent has stopped, so the message waits until you continue it with the command the line names: the agent's own command for an agent of a config, and `dockingbird start --as NAME` for one of the default environment, whose own terminal can't read messages. The not-running form: the agent's start began but no container of it runs (that start stopped before its container ran), so the message waits until it starts; the command the line names starts it. The still-starting form: another command is starting the agent right now, and the message reaches it once its container runs. The group form: you sent with `--all`, `--role` or `--swarm` (or `--swarm` with `--role`), and one message went to every live agent of that group; the line counts them. A group with no live agent is refused, so a message never goes to nobody.

```text
Sent {kind} to {name} (message {value}).
```

Or:

```text
Sent {kind} to {name} (message {value}).
{name} has ended; it gets this when you continue it: dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
Sent {kind} to {name} (message {value}).
{name} isn't running yet; it gets this once it starts: dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}
```

Or:

```text
Sent {kind} to {name} (message {value}).
{name} is still starting; it gets this once its container runs.
```

Or:

```text
Sent {kind} to {count:agent|agents}, {group} (message {value}).
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- none, where the message only informs
- dockingbird {subcommand} --as {name}

Exit status: 0 (done).

text:

heading: Configs, connections and host resources > CONNECT_DATABASE_REFUSED
summary: `dockingbird connect --database` checked the database from Dockingbird's own side and refused it; the connection was removed again and nothing is kept.
text:
When: `dockingbird connect --database` checked the database from Dockingbird's own side and refused it; the connection was removed again and nothing is kept. One line shows the cause. The role can write: itself (the role it logs in as, whatever role it becomes on connecting), or through a role it can switch to (a superuser, a role that can create roles or databases, replicate or bypass row security, a role that can write, one that reads or writes the server's files, runs its programs, ends other connections, runs maintenance or forces a checkpoint, or a member of any of them), or it owns a table or the database, or has the MAINTAIN right on a table, or it may call the function that writes a message into the server's log of changes or, in any schema, one of the `dblink` extension's that opens a second connection outside the read-only transaction, one that exports a large object to the server's files or imports one from them, one that switches the server's log of changes to a new file or marks a restore point in it, or one that resets the server's statistics; the message shows the commands that make a read-only role that is a member of none of those, owns no table, has no MAINTAIN right and is not the database's owner, and, where the `dblink` extension is installed, the REVOKE that takes its three functions from every role (or drop the extension). On PostgreSQL 16 and earlier the function that writes into the log of changes has no fourth parameter, so name its two forms without it in the REVOKE line. Or Dockingbird couldn't reach the server: is it listening for connections from Docker, and does its list of allowed hosts let them in? The same line shows when the server took longer than a query's time limit to answer the check, as a busy server may: run the command again once it answers. Or the server asks for a password none was given for. Or it refused the role, its password or the database name, which PostgreSQL doesn't tell apart. Or it allows prepared transactions, which a query could leave behind: set their maximum to 0 in its configuration and restart it.

```text
The role {value} can write to {target}, so Dockingbird won't give it to agents.
Make a read-only role: CREATE ROLE reader LOGIN;
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE {name} TO reader;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO reader;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO reader;
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION
  pg_catalog.pg_logical_emit_message(
    boolean, text, text, boolean),
  pg_catalog.pg_logical_emit_message(
    boolean, text, bytea, boolean)
FROM PUBLIC;
If the database has the dblink extension, also run this, with its
schema on the search path (or drop the extension):
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION
  dblink(text), dblink(text, text),
  dblink(text, boolean),
  dblink(text, text, boolean),
  dblink_exec(text), dblink_exec(text, text),
  dblink_exec(text, boolean),
  dblink_exec(text, text, boolean),
  dblink_connect(text),
  dblink_connect(text, text)
FROM PUBLIC;
Then run this again with reader.
```

Or:

```text
Dockingbird couldn't reach {target} from its container.
Is the server listening for connections from Docker (listen_addresses,
pg_hba.conf)? Then run this again.
```

Or:

```text
{target} asks for a password for {value}.
Run this again with --password.
```

Or:

```text
{target} refused the role, its password or the database name.
Check the three, then run this again with --password.
```

Or:

```text
{target} allows prepared transactions, which a query could
leave behind, so Dockingbird won't use it.
Set max_prepared_transactions = 0 in postgresql.conf, restart the server,
then run this again.
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- Then run this again with reader.
- Then run this again.
- Run this again with --password.
- Check the three, then run this again with --password.
- Set max_prepared_transactions = 0 in postgresql.conf, restart the server, then run this again.

Exit status: 1 (a problem Dockingbird printed).

heading: Configs, connections and host resources > BROWSER_SOLVER_CHANNEL_FAILED
summary: The solve watcher of an agent's browser could not reach what a solve needs, and its log carries this line.
text:
When: The solve watcher of an agent's browser could not reach what a solve needs, and its log carries this line. Either the browser's container could not open the channel for the next challenge (the browser was started without a solver, or its service is gone), and the watcher ended: the agent's browser runs on with no solver. Or one connection of your solver to the browser could not be bridged (the browser is gone, or docker could not be started): that connection was closed and the solve went on to its outcome. Or the outcome of a solve could not be handed back, the channel being gone by then: the agent's browser was told the solve failed, and the watcher went on to the next challenge.

```text
The agent's browser can't hand its challenge to a solver: {detail}.
```

Next step: none; it only informs.

summary: You started an agent whose config installs Chrome Web Store extensions in its browser, with egress `none`.
text:

```text
update hosts, and this start's egress is none.
Start with egress allowlist, models or full, or remove the store entries from
the config and add it again.
```

heading: Benchmark jobs > HARBOR_OPTION_REFUSED
summary: You gave `dockingbird harbor run` an option Dockingbird doesn't pass on to Harbor, and nothing ran.
text:
When: You gave `dockingbird harbor run` an option Dockingbird doesn't pass on to Harbor, and nothing ran. Dockingbird passes only the options of Harbor's `run` it knows, and refuses by name the ones that mount folders of this Mac into the task's container (`--mounts`, `--mounts-json`) or replace the environment Dockingbird runs jobs in (`--environment-import-path`); the ones that would run a task or a dataset it hasn't checked (a job config, a dataset, another task or a repository); `--env-file`, which would change the environment it gives Harbor; the ones that change the classes Harbor runs the job with (a plugin, a verifier, a simulated user, environment keywords); the ones that send the job to Harbor Hub or Hugging Face; `--override-gpus` and `--override-tpu`, which would give the container a device of this computer; `--ae` or `--ve` with a key, token, password or other credential in the variable's name, which would land on a command line and in the trial's logs (save it with `dockingbird login` instead); and any option it doesn't know at this Harbor commit. `baseline`, which runs oracle then nop and names both jobs itself, also refuses `-a`, `--agent-import-path` and `--job-name`, and a `-k` that isn't a whole number of one or more. Both `run` and `baseline` also refuse `-k`, `-n`, `--n-concurrent-agents` or `-r` over the count the message names, and more `-m` models than that: a job that big wouldn't finish on this Mac (give a smaller number, or leave the option out). Give the option a value, or leave it out.

```text
Run the job without it.
```

heading: Benchmark jobs > HARBOR_SIGNIN_TOO_SHORT
summary: You ran `dockingbird harbor run -a claude-code` with no saved Claude key or token, and the Claude sign-in on this Mac isn't known to last the whole trial.
text:
When: You ran `dockingbird harbor run -a claude-code` with no saved Claude key or token, and the Claude sign-in on this Mac isn't known to last the whole trial. Claude Code in a trial never picks up a sign-in that renews while it runs, so the sign-in must outlast the task's agent timeout, its build timeout, Harbor's setup and a margin, for every wave of its attempts (`-k` attempts, `-n` at a time, each retried `-r` times), with the verifier's timeout and a retry's wait between one run and the next; the message says how long it has and how long the trial needs (or that the trial needs a little more than the sign-in has, when the two would read alike), or that the trial would need it for longer than the bound the message names, or that the task sets no agent timeout, or that a timeout multiplier you gave leaves it no finite time bound, or that the sign-in names no expiry. Nothing ran. Save a long-lived token (`claude setup-token`, then `dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -`) and trials use it.

```text
Your Claude sign-in on this Mac is good for {has}, and this trial needs {needs}.
Save a long-lived token: claude setup-token, then dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -
```

Or:

```text
Your Claude sign-in on this Mac is good for {has}, and this trial
needs a little more than that.
Save a long-lived token: claude setup-token, then dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -
```

Or:

```text
This trial would need your Claude sign-in for more than
{longest}, so no sign-in is known to cover it.
Save a long-lived token: claude setup-token, then dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -
```

Or:

```text
This task sets no finite [agent] timeout_sec, so no sign-in is
known to cover it.
Save a long-lived token: claude setup-token, then dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -
```

Or:

```text
With a timeout multiplier you gave, this trial has no finite
time bound, so no sign-in is known to cover it.
Save a long-lived token: claude setup-token, then dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -
```

Or:

```text
Your Claude sign-in on this Mac has no expiry Dockingbird can
read, so it isn't known to cover this trial.
Save a long-lived token: claude setup-token, then dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -
```

Next step: Save a long-lived token: claude setup-token, then dockingbird login claude --oauth-token -

text:
When: mise couldn't install a version the repo names (a version that doesn't exist, a download that failed, a checksum that didn't match), or the install ended before it finished. The message shows mise's last lines, and no agent was started: fix the file that names the version, or start with the image's versions using `--no-toolchain`. After `dockingbird env install` or `dockingbird env lock`, run it again.

```text
Couldn't install {tools:and}. Its last lines:
{tail}
Fix the file that names the version, or start with the image's
versions: dockingbird {tool} --no-toolchain
```

Or:

```text
Couldn't install {tools:and}. Its last lines:
{tail}
mise.lock doesn't name what the repo asks for now, and a start can't
change it. Lock it, then start again: dockingbird env lock
```

Or:

```text
The install of {tools:and} ended before it finished. Its last lines:
{tail}
Run this again, or: dockingbird {tool} --no-toolchain
```

Or:

```text
Couldn't install {tools:and}. Its last lines:
{tail}
Run this again.
```

Or:

```text
Couldn't install {tools:and}. Its last lines:
{tail}
mise.lock doesn't name what the repo asks for now, and env install can't
change it. Lock it instead, which installs too: dockingbird env lock
```

Or:

```text
The install of {tools:and} ended before it finished. Run this again.
```

Next step, as the message gives it:

- dockingbird {tool} --no-toolchain
- dockingbird env lock
- Run this again.

heading: Homes, checkouts and toolchains > TOOLCHAIN_LOOK_FAILED
summary: mise couldn't read the repo's tool versions, such as from a `mise.toml` that isn't valid, and the message shows what mise said.
text:
When: mise couldn't read the repo's tool versions, such as from a `mise.toml` that isn't valid, and the message shows what mise said. When the checkout is marked untrusted (`dockingbird trust --off`) and its mise config needs trust, it says so and offers `dockingbird trust`. A start can still go ahead with the image's versions using `--no-toolchain`.

```text
Couldn't read {repo}'s toolchain. Its last lines:
{tail}
Fix what it says, or start with the image's
versions: dockingbird {tool} --no-toolchain
```

Or:

```text
Couldn't read {repo}'s toolchain. Its last lines:
{tail}
Fix what it says and run this again.
```

Or:

```text
Couldn't read {repo}'s toolchain: its mise config needs trust and
this checkout is untrusted. mise said:
{tail}
Trust the checkout: dockingbird trust, or start with the image's versions:
dockingbird {tool} --no-toolchain
```

Or:

```text
Couldn't read {repo}'s toolchain: its mise config needs trust and
this checkout is untrusted. mise said:
{tail}
Trust the checkout: dockingbird trust, then run this again.
```

heading: Commands
summary: Each table lists the commands of one group with their arguments, one line of purpose, the exit statuses they end with and the page that explains them.
text:
Each table lists the commands of one group with their arguments, one line of purpose, the exit statuses they end with and the page that explains them.
Statuses 0, 1 and 2 are on every command, and [exit-codes.md](integration/exit-codes.md) explains 69, 77, 78 and the tool's own.
`dockingbird COMMAND -h` prints the same arguments from the installed release, and the unlisted `fleet`, `work` and `inspect swarm` commands are included here.

heading: Commands > Global options
summary: For `claude` and `codex` the global options go before the tool's name, as in `dockingbird --verbose claude`, because everything after it belongs to the tool.
text:
| Option | Where it goes | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | before the command | prints every message as one line of JSON, an envelope; see [json.md](integration/json.md) |
| `--verbose` | before the command | adds ids, codes, paths and timings, and shows each message's id in brackets such as `[NOTHING_NEEDS_YOU]` |
| `--home NAME` | before the command | runs in the home `homes/NAME` of the default home; refused with exit 2 when `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME` is also set; see [home-layout.md](files/home-layout.md) |
| `-h`, `--help` | alone, or after any command | prints the help; under `--json` it is an envelope whose `id` is `HELP` |
| `-v`, `--version` | alone | prints the versions of Dockingbird, Claude Code and Codex, and marks a pinned one |

For `claude` and `codex` the global options go before the tool's name, as in `dockingbird --verbose claude`, because everything after it belongs to the tool.
After a command, `--home NAME` belongs to `--host` on `status`, `swarm` and `inspect`, and names a home of that host.

heading: Commands > Everyday
text:
| Command | Arguments | What it does | Exit | Guide |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `claude` | `[--as NAME] [--new] [--egress MODE] [--cpus N] [--memory SIZE] [--no-toolchain] [--no-deps] [--agent-md PATH] [--claude-md PATH] [--skills PATHS] [--harness-config PATH] [-- TOOL ARGS]` | starts Claude Code on this repo in its own container, picks up kept work, or reconnects to a running agent | the tool's own, 1, 2 | [daily-loop.md](../guides/daily-loop.md) |

| `codex` | the same as `claude`; `--claude-md` is refused | starts Codex on this repo in its own container, picks up kept work, or reconnects to a running agent | the tool's own, 1, 2 | [daily-loop.md](../guides/daily-loop.md) |

| `status` | `[NAME] [--host NAME] [--home NAME]` | shows who works on what, what was shared today and what needs you; with a name, one agent; reads only | 0, 1, 2 | [daily-loop.md](../guides/daily-loop.md) |

| `sync` | `[--accept COMMIT] [--let-go]` | takes the agents' commits on your branch and sends yours; `--accept` resumes after a pause, `--let-go` makes your branch the one after you refused a deleted branch's commits | 0, 1, 2 | [daily-loop.md](../guides/daily-loop.md) |

| `stop` | `[NAME ...] [--yes]` | stops the named agents, or every agent and Dockingbird itself; nothing is lost | 0, 1, 2 | [daily-loop.md](../guides/daily-loop.md) |

| `init` | `[--project SLUG] [--check] [--force] [--no-register]` | makes this repo ready: the project file, rules, an example swarm, skills and agent definitions; `--check` writes nothing and exits 1 when files are not this release's | 0, 1, 2 | [first-run.md](../getting-started/first-run.md) |

| `login` | `TOOL [--here] [--api-key [--base-url URL]]`, `claude --oauth-token - [--base-url URL]`, `codex --auth-json -` | signs in again or as someone else; TOOL is `claude` or `codex`; the last login wins | 0, 1, 2 | [sign-in-and-api-keys.md](../guides/sign-in-and-api-keys.md) |

| `logout` | `TOOL` | signs the tool out and removes its saved API key; your own sign-ins are untouched | 0, 1, 2 | [sign-in-and-api-keys.md](../guides/sign-in-and-api-keys.md) |

| `trust` | `[PATH] [--off] [--forget]` | marks a repo trusted, or with `--off` keeps its own settings, hooks and MCP servers off on this computer; `--forget` is `--off` | 0, 1, 2 | [trust-and-repo-settings.md](../guides/trust-and-repo-settings.md) |

| `egress` | `[MODE] [--allow ENTRY]...`, `--reset` | shows or sets what new agents may reach: `allowlist`, `models`, `none` or `full` | 0, 1, 2 | [egress-and-network.md](../guides/egress-and-network.md) |

summary: Each `swarm` action changes this home's record only: no agent starts, stops or is told.
text:
| `set` | `NAME [--model MODEL] [--effort LEVEL] [--compact-at POINT] [--harness-config PATH] [--skills PATHS] [--stop-after-turn] [--run-turns]` | changes a running bus agent's model, effort, compact point or tool settings file from its next turn; `--skills`, given alone, adds skills to a running agent; `--stop-after-turn` ends it after its running turn | 0, 1, 2 | [delegating-tasks.md](../guides/delegating-tasks.md) |

| `swarm remove` | `NAME` | takes an agent out of its swarm | 0, 1, 2 | [swarms.md](../guides/swarms.md) |

| `swarm role` | `NAME --role ROLE` | changes an agent's role in its swarm | 0, 1, 2 | [swarms.md](../guides/swarms.md) |

Each `swarm` action changes this home's record only: no agent starts, stops or is told.
`swarm` also takes `--host NAME`, `--home NAME` and `--json`.

heading: Exit codes
summary: Every dockingbird command ends with one exit status, also called an exit code, and under `--json` the last envelope repeats it as `exit_code` ([the envelope](json.md)).
text:
Every dockingbird command ends with one exit status, also called an exit code, and under `--json` the last envelope repeats it as `exit_code` ([the envelope](json.md)).
A message's id says what happened and its status says how the command ended, so a script reads both; [the catalogue](../../troubleshooting.md) lists every id.
`ok` in the envelope is `true` only when the status is 0.

| Status | Meaning | When | What a script does |

|---|---|---|---|

| 0 | done | the command did what was asked, or had nothing to do (`stop` and `clean` on a computer that is not set up) | goes on |

| 1 | a problem Dockingbird printed, with its next step | a refused start, a `sync` that could not do what was asked, `init --check` finding a file that is not the running release's, `clean` with no terminal to ask on, a `fleet update` step that failed | reads `id` and `next_step` from the envelope, runs the next step or stops, and never repeats the same command unchanged |

| 2 | usage | a word, an option or a value the command does not take: a bad `--as` name, `--home` together with `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME`, a `DOCKINGBIRD_` variable no command reads, a `fleet update` refused before it runs (a release tag that does not exist, a host with no `repoint` line) | fixes the command line, since a retry cannot succeed |

| the tool's own | `dockingbird claude` and `dockingbird codex` end with Claude Code's or Codex's status once the tool has started; 0 when the agent keeps working without a terminal; 1 when Dockingbird stopped before starting it | the tool's own run ended | treats the status as the tool's result; a tool that exits 3 gives an envelope with `"ok": false` and `"exit_code": 3` |

| 69 | the organisation's store did not answer | a fleet scheduler command whose database is down, restarting or out of connections; the message names the database's host, the role tried and the connection's own words | retries after a delay and checks the network and the database; a `fleet worker` or `fleet admitter` under a service manager exits 69 and is started again by it |

heading: Exit codes
summary: A script treats exit code 78 as "log in first": it runs the `org login` line the message names and repeats the command.
text:
| 77 | a login the store's roles refuse for this command | `org create` by a role that is not a member of `fleet_admin`; `fleet update` by a login that is not a member; `fleet submit` or `fleet run` by a person who is not a member of the project's group, with nothing recorded | asks an admin to run `dockingbird org members add PERSON --project SLUG`, or runs the command as `fleet_admin` |

| 78 | a fleet refusal: no usable login | no org login on this computer; a kind of command with no role in `org.toml`; a role with no line in `~/.pgpass`; a login the database turns down (wrong password, a role or database it lacks) or an error code once connected; a `fleet.toml` that holds a `password` | runs the login the message names, `dockingbird org login HOST --as user --role ROLE`, then repeats the command |

A script treats exit code 78 as "log in first": it runs the `org login` line the message names and repeats the command. Exit code 77 means the login is not the admin's. Exit code 69 means the store did not answer.

`fleet run` ends with the status of the command it ran, 124 when its `--bound` interrupts the command, and 1 when no lease was taken within `--wait`.
The scheduler's login and role rules are in [the org file](../files/org-file.md) and [the team fleet guide](../../guides/team-fleet.md).
