heading: Role and connection files
summary: A role library holds the settings a swarm role reuses, and a service connection file says what a brokered program runs and what an agent may choose.
text: A role library holds the settings a swarm role reuses, and a service connection file says what a brokered program runs and what an agent may choose. Both live in your repository's `.dockingbird/` folder. [The swarm definition reference](swarm-definition.md) shows how a role names a library file, and [the cookbook on role libraries](../../../examples/swarm-from-a-role-library/README.md) uses both.

heading: Role and connection files > Library role file
summary: `.dockingbird/roles/NAME.toml` is a role a definition names with `use = "NAME"`, and `use = "dockingbird/NAME"` names the shipped file of that name.
text:
`.dockingbird/roles/NAME.toml` is a role a definition names with `use = "NAME"`, and `use = "dockingbird/NAME"` names the shipped file of that name. Paths in it are relative to `.dockingbird/roles/`. `{{name}}` expands in its string values and its texts, a parameter of the definition or a built-in such as `{{swarm}}`, whether or not the definition declares `[params]`.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | slug | optional; when given, the file's own name, else `use-name` |
| `harness` | `claude` or `codex` | the tool the agents run |
| `model`, `effort` | string | the role's model and effort; the shipped roles name neither, so the project file or your organisation's store gives them |
| `brief` | path | the Markdown file of the first task |
| `instructions` | path | text added after Dockingbird's rules and the project's, never in place of them |
| `connections` | list of names | the home's connections its agents are granted at start |
| `subagents` | table | one helper kind, `[subagents.NAME]`; a role takes one kind at most |
| `workspace`, `egress`, `allow`, `env` | as in a config | session settings |
| `context` | `kept` or `fresh` | one conversation for every delivery, or a new one for each task delivery |
| `tools` | as in a config | A config takes `bus` (messages and files, the default), `default` (claims and commits) or `full` (both); a swarm role takes `bus`, `full` or a list that keeps every bus tool |
| `harness_config` | a path, or a table by harness | the harness's own settings file, relative to `.dockingbird/roles/`; never expanded |
| `needs` | cpus, memory, pids | the role's resource reservation |
| `compact_at` | `500000`, `500k` or `auto` | the point at which the agent's context compacts |
| `session_hours` | integer, 1 to 168 | how long each agent may run |
| `skills` | table of `path` and `into` | skills its agents' tool lists as its own, as a config's `[skills]` takes them; each `path` is from the top of the swarm's source, not from `.dockingbird/roles/`; see [skills.md](../../guides/skills.md) |
| `[fallback]`, `[fallback.on]` | tables | the tool its agents move to after a failed turn, and each error class's rule, as a config's `[fallback]` takes them; see [app-config.md](app-config.md#keys-of-fallback) |

heading: Role and connection files > Library role file
summary: A `[[role]]` entry that uses the file replaces each key it gives.
text:
A `[[role]]` entry that uses the file replaces each key it gives. `needs` and each `[subagents.NAME]` table merge field by field instead, the entry's field winning. An entry's `skills` or `fallback` replaces the file's whole table.

| Not allowed in a library file | Why |
|---|---|
| `use`, `count`, `min`, `max`, `send_to`, `reviews`, `tests`, `kind`, `args` | they belong to a swarm's own `[[role]]` |
| `system_prompt`, `append_system_prompt`, `developer_instructions`, `rules` | they would change a layer Dockingbird injects, so they are refused (`fixed-prompt`) |

heading: Role and connection files > The library's index
summary: `.dockingbird/roles/index.toml` lists the library's roles and the names a role is looked up by.
text:
`.dockingbird/roles/index.toml` lists the library's roles and the names a role is looked up by. `dockingbird init` installs the shipped one.

```toml
roles = ["coordinator", "implementer", "reviewer", "tester", "reader", "hands"]

[defaults]
reviews = "reviewer"
tests = "tester"
otherwise = "implementer"
```

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `roles` | the library's roles; `init` writes one `[roles.NAME]` table into `.dockingbird/project.toml` for each |
| `[defaults]` `reviews` | the name a role that reviews and names no `kind` looks its model and effort up by |
| `[defaults]` `tests` | the same for a role that tests |
| `[defaults]` `otherwise` | the same for every other role |

The shipped index is read first, and the project's replaces each key it gives. An empty value in the project's `[defaults]` gives no name for that kind of role, so such a role needs a model and an effort from another source. A `use` reads the role's file by its name, whether or not `roles` lists it.

heading: Role and connection files > Subagent block
summary: `[subagents.NAME]` is one helper that the role's harness runs, with its own settings.
text:
`[subagents.NAME]` is one helper that the role's harness runs, with its own settings. A role holds one such table at most (`one-subagent-kind`).

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `instructions` | path | required; the helper's own text; the first line is the helper's description |
| `model` | string | the helper's model; left out, the role's own |
| `effort` | string | the helper's effort; left out, the tool's default |
| `max` | integer, 0 to 20 | how many helpers run at once; `0` denies the helper tool; left out, the tool's own cap |
| `tools` | list of tool names | the tool's own tools the helper may use; left out, the role's |

heading: Role and connection files > Service connection file
summary: `.dockingbird/connections/NAME.toml` is registered with `dockingbird connect NAME --service FILE`.
text:
`.dockingbird/connections/NAME.toml` is registered with `dockingbird connect NAME --service FILE`. The file must be yours, readable by you alone, not a link and not inside `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME`. `connect` checks every key, that `argv` uses each argument the file declares, and that the checkout is at its commit. It runs nothing.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `program` | absolute path | the program that runs, with `argv` |
| `checkout` | absolute path | the program's checkout; give it with `commit` or give neither |
| `commit` | string | the commit the checkout must be at; `serve` refuses to run once the checkout moved |
| `timeout_s` | integer | the most seconds one run may take, then it is stopped |
| `argv` | list of words | the program's words; `{output}` stands once for the output folder and each `{NAME}` for an argument |
| `uses` | list with one name | a database connection of the home whose credential each run gets as `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGDATABASE`, `PGUSER` and `PGPASSWORD`, never in a file, a log or an agent |
| `[call]` | table | in place of `argv`, a Python function in the checkout |
| `[call]` `python` | path | the interpreter, relative to the checkout |
| `[call]` `module` | string | the module that holds the function |
| `[call]` `function` | string | the function; it is called with the checked arguments as keyword arguments, and its return value, as JSON, is the run's `result.json` |

heading: Role and connection files > Argument keys
summary: Each argument the agent may choose is a table `[arguments.NAME]`, or an inline table under `[arguments]`.
text:
Each argument the agent may choose is a table `[arguments.NAME]`, or an inline table under `[arguments]`.

| Key | Used by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | all | `int`, `text` or `choice` |
| `minimum` | `int` | the lowest whole number allowed |
| `maximum` | `int` | the highest whole number allowed |
| `choices` | `choice` | the list of words the agent may pick |
| `max_chars` | `text` | the longest text allowed |

A `text` argument reaches the program as the agent typed it. A program that reads one as a path or a command name gives the agent that reach, so declare `choice` or `int` where the program takes a path, a name or a mode.

heading: Role and connection files > How a run behaves
text:
| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| process | the program alone, never through a shell, in its checkout |
| environment | `PATH`, your `HOME`, `LANG=C.UTF-8`, a `TMPDIR` of its own and `DOCKINGBIRD_SERVICE_OUTPUT`, the output folder's path |
| timeout | past `timeout_s` it gets `SIGTERM`, then `SIGKILL` 10 seconds later |
| output | the output folder is the result, with `stdout.txt` and `stderr.txt`, at most 64 MiB and 10,000 entries, links left out |
| where it lands | in the asking agent's log folder under `log/connections/<job>/` |
| who runs it | `dockingbird serve NAME`, as you, one request at a time, oldest first |

heading: What dockingbird init writes
summary: Run `dockingbird init` anywhere in a repo and it writes a project file, a rules file, an example swarm, the skills of the release, the agent definitions, and a lock file that lists each installed file with its digest.
text:
Run `dockingbird init` anywhere in a repo and it writes a project file, a rules file, an example swarm, the skills of the release, the agent definitions, and a lock file that lists each installed file with its digest.
Commit all of them with `git add .dockingbird .agents .claude && git commit`, so every clone of the repo has the same set-up.

heading: What dockingbird init writes > The files
summary: A file you edited is kept and named, and `--force` replaces it.
text:
| Path | What it holds | Later runs of `init` |
|---|---|---|
| `.dockingbird/project.toml` | the project's file; keys below | adds a `[roles.NAME]` table for each role of the library's `index.toml` the file lacks, and changes nothing else |
| `.dockingbird/rules.md` | the lines every agent of the project gets after Dockingbird's own rules; an agent's whole rules text may be 64 KB at most | never rewritten |
| `.dockingbird/swarms/example/` | an example swarm; fill its `[placement] hosts` from `dockingbird fleet hosts`, then `dockingbird fleet submit .dockingbird/swarms/example` | never rewritten |
| `.dockingbird/roles/` | the role library: `index.toml` and one file for each shipped role (`coordinator`, `implementer`, `reviewer`, `tester`, `reader` and `hands`) with its texts, which you edit freely; see [roles-and-connections.md](roles-and-connections.md) | changed only where a new release changed a file you have not edited; `--force` replaces an edited one |
| `.agents/skills/` | this release's skills | changed only where a new release changed a file |
| `.claude/skills` | a link to `../.agents/skills` | kept |
| `.claude/agents/` | this release's agent definitions | changed only where a new release changed a file |
| `.dockingbird/skills.lock` | every file `init` installed, each with its digest and its source; it names no release | changes with the files it lists; a lock in the older format, which named a release, counts as out of date for `init --check`, and the next `init` rewrites it once |

A file you edited is kept and named, and `--force` replaces it.
`init` writes nothing through a link: a `.dockingbird`, `.agents` or `.claude` that is a link, or a `.claude/skills` that links anywhere but `../.agents/skills`, stops it before anything is written.

heading: What dockingbird init writes > Keys of project.toml
summary: `slug` and `version` are required; every other key is optional.
text:
`slug` and `version` are required; every other key is optional.
A key or a table outside this list is refused, and the refusal names the key.
A swarm role's lookup name is its `kind`, else `reviewer`, `tester` or `implementer` by what it does; [the definition reference](swarm-definition.md#where-a-roles-model-and-effort-come-from) gives the whole order.

| Key | Values | Default | What it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | `1` | `1` | the file's format; another number is refused |
| `slug` | lowercase letters, digits and `-` | `--project SLUG`, else the name of the repo's `origin` remote, else its folder's | the project's name in your organisation's store |
| `release` | text | the release that ran `init` | the release whose `init` wrote the file and its skills |
| `[org] ops_repository` | `owner/name` | empty | written empty by `init`; leave it empty |
| `[checks] runner_host` | a host name of `hosts.toml` | empty | written empty by `init`; leave it empty |
| `[checks] runner_script` | a path in the repo | empty | written empty by `init`; leave it empty |
| `[rules] file` | a path in the repo | `.dockingbird/rules.md` | the project's rules file, read at every start; a file that is missing, a link, not UTF-8 text or holding a Dockingbird credential stops the start |
| `[roles.NAME] harness` | `claude` or `codex` | `claude` | the tool a swarm role looked up by `NAME` runs when its definition names none; the table's model and effort apply only to a role on this tool; `init` writes one table for each role of the library's `index.toml`, and you may add a table under any lowercase name |
| `[roles.NAME] model` | the tool's model word | empty | the model of a role looked up by `NAME` that names none itself; empty means the organisation's store row of `NAME` and the role's tool, else `fleet submit` refuses the role |
| `[roles.NAME] effort` | the tool's effort word | empty | the same for the effort; empty means the store's row, else `fleet submit` refuses the role |
| `[lint] forbidden` | list of words | none | words this repository refuses, each a non-empty single line |

heading: What dockingbird init writes > Registering the project
text:
| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| an org login on this computer | `init` adds the project to your organisation's store as your `user` role: its slug, the `origin` remote's address, the default branch and this release, once; a later run says the store has it |
| a login that is not an admin, a store that is not made yet, or a store that does not answer | the line names the cause and `init` still ends 0 |
| no org login | the line says to log in first with `dockingbird org login HOST --as user --role ROLE` |
| `--no-register` | skips the step |

heading: What dockingbird init writes > Messages
text:
| Id | When |
|---|---|
| [INIT_DONE](../../troubleshooting.md#init_done) | the first run wrote the files |
| [INIT_CURRENT](../../troubleshooting.md#init_current) | everything is already this release's |
| [INIT_OUT_OF_DATE](../../troubleshooting.md#init_out_of_date) | `init --check` found files that are not this release's; exit 1 |
| [INIT_FILE_EDITED](../../troubleshooting.md#init_file_edited) | a file you edited was kept |
| [INIT_PROJECT_FILE_INVALID](../../troubleshooting.md#init_project_file_invalid) | `project.toml` has a key or value Dockingbird does not read |
| [RULES_FILE_MISSING](../../troubleshooting.md#rules_file_missing) | `[rules] file` names a file that is not there, so no agent starts |

heading: The home folder layout
summary: A Dockingbird home is one folder on your computer, `~/.local/share/dockingbird` by default, plus five Docker volumes that never appear in Finder or in your file listings.
text:
A Dockingbird home is one folder on your computer, `~/.local/share/dockingbird` by default, plus five Docker volumes that never appear in Finder or in your file listings.
Dockingbird never writes into a folder that lacks the marker file, and `dockingbird clean --all` removes nothing from such a folder.
The folder itself has mode 0700.

heading: The home folder layout > The home folder and DOCKINGBIRD_HOME
text:
| Path | What it holds | Mode |

|---|---|---|

| `.dockingbird-home` | the marker: a small JSON file Dockingbird writes first into a new home; never a link | 0600 |

| `config.toml` | the image tag, the last build's duration (`last_build_seconds`, the next build's estimate) and, yours, a `trust =` line | |

| `egress.toml` | optional; what new agents may reach, written by `dockingbird egress` | 0600 |

| `versions.toml` | optional; which version each tool runs, written by `dockingbird pin` or by you | |

| `instructions/claude.md`, `instructions/codex.md` | optional, yours; rules for every agent of that tool in this home | |

| `repos.toml` | each checkout: its display name, path, repo name, branches and their root commits | |

| `hosts.toml` | the other computers you reach; see [hosts-file.md](hosts-file.md) | 0600 when Dockingbird writes it |

| `fleet.toml` | optional, yours; the older form of the fleet database login, see [org-file.md](org-file.md) | 0600 |

| `trust/`, `untrusted/` | the marks `dockingbird trust` and `trust --off` leave for a checkout | |

| `homes/NAME/` | another home on this computer, made by `--home NAME` | |

| `clones/` | a fleet worker's clones of the repositories its swarms work on | |

| `installs/RELEASE/` | a release installed for a home's program file to name | |

| `installs/current` | a link to the release this computer's fleet worker and admitter run; `dockingbird fleet update` moves it | |

| `cache/`, `org-db/` | reserved; `clean --all` of this home keeps these folders and says so | |

| `state.json` | a cache no container can write; its absence means "not set up" | |

| `program` | one line: the path of the `dockingbird` script a start or update ran; `fleet scrape` and `fleet read-home` run it for this home | 0600 |

| `locks/`, `attach/` | the setup lock, the link locks and `hosts.lock`; one attach lock per agent shown in a terminal | |

| `docker-config/config.json` | the docker configuration every docker call of Dockingbird runs with; it holds no logins | 0600 |

| `results/AGENT/` | the files `dockingbird results` saved, one folder per agent | 0700, files 0600 |

| `connections/ID.json` | the catalogue `dockingbird connect` saved for one connection: each repo, branch and key path; a key's copy lives in a Docker volume, never here | 0700 |

heading: The home folder layout > The home folder and DOCKINGBIRD_HOME
text:
| `configs/NAME/` | a config you added: its copy, `config.toml` and the files it names | 0700, files 0600 |

| `configs/index.json` | the list of the configs you added | 0600 |

| `vaults/` | the password stores a vault connection reads | 0700 |

| `logs/coordinator.log` | the log of the coordinator, the background process that Dockingbird turns off after 30 idle minutes | |

| `logs/agents/NAME-STAMP.log` | each agent's log, copied when it ends, with control characters escaped | |

| `logs/dockingbird.log` | an unexpected error's details, redacted; rotated to `.1` | |

| `tmp/` | sync bundles in flight; empty between commands | |

| `bin/dockingbird-gui` | the GUI that `dockingbird ui` runs; not yet available, so the file is not there | |

| `bin/zeusfyi-license`, `bin/zeusfyi-license.fetch-failed` | the license client, downloaded once, and the time of its last failed download | 0700 |

| `license.json` | the license client's file: the license, this computer's id and label, the last check-in, the terms accepted; `clean --all` gives the seat back, then removes it | 0600 |

| `completion/dockingbird.SHELL` | the tab completion script `completion --install` wrote; `dockingbird update` keeps it current | 0700, files 0600 |

| `update/previous/`, `update/stage.json`, `update/last-switch.json` | a staged update: the copy of the version your agents run, what is staged, and the last switch; `clean --all` removes all three | 0700 |

| `toolchain/store.json` | the toolchain store's last listing, which `dockingbird env` and `clean` read | 0700, files 0600 |

| `toolchain/resolved/KEY.toml` | each checkout's last look at the versions its agents get; KEY is the SHA-256 of its real path | 0700, files 0600 |

| `fleet/container/` | the credential of a computer that joined a control plane; never in an agent's container, a log or a command line | |

| `apt-pool/` in `~/.local/share/dockingbird/` | the copy of the pinned Ubuntu package files the image installs, shared by every home of your user on that computer | |

heading: The home folder layout > The small files you edit
text:
| File | Keys | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `config.toml` | `trust = "untrusted"` or `trust = "trusted"` | what a checkout with no mark is; no line means `"trusted"`; any other value is refused by every command that reads trust, and Dockingbird changes no byte of the file but its `last_build_seconds` line |
| `egress.toml` | `egress = "MODE"`, `allow = [...]` | `MODE` is `allowlist`, `models`, `none` or `full`; `allow` appears only with `allowlist` |
| `versions.toml` | `claude = "2.1.285"`, `codex = "0.162.1"` | a version Dockingbird downloads if it lacks it; `"latest"` or no line follows the latest release; `"stable"` is Claude Code's slower channel and works for Claude only; any other line, an unknown key or a file that is not plain TOML of yours stops the command and names the line |
| `instructions/claude.md`, `instructions/codex.md` | Markdown | Dockingbird copies a changed file into Docker the way it copies a key, read-only to agents, and never mounts it |

heading: The home folder layout > Docker volumes, kept by Docker and named with a `-ID` suffix in a second installation
text:
| Volume | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `dockingbird-state` | the database, the tokens, the agents' protected copies of each linked branch and every agent's own copy |
| `dockingbird-tools` | the program store: each downloaded version of Claude Code and Codex |
| `dockingbird-home-claude` | Claude's credentials store, its saved API key and your rules' copy |
| `dockingbird-home-codex` | Codex's credentials store, its saved API key and your rules' copy |
| `dockingbird-browser-sock-NAME` | one per agent whose config asks for a browser; removed once the agent's container is gone |

heading: The home folder layout > In your checkout
text:
| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `.git/config`, `branch.BRANCH.dockingbird` | one line per linked branch; `git branch -m` moves it with the branch and `clean --all` removes it |
| `refs/remotes/dockingbird/BRANCH` | the head the agents' copy started from, then their commits as of your last sync; `clean --all` removes it |
| `.dockingbird/`, `.agents/`, `.claude/` | what `dockingbird init` writes; see [project-file.md](project-file.md) |

heading: The home folder layout > A second home on the same computer
summary: `--home NAME` before a command runs it in the home `homes/NAME` of the default home's folder.
text:
`--home NAME` before a command runs it in the home `homes/NAME` of the default home's folder.
The first command that claims it, such as `dockingbird --home lab egress full`, makes the folder, `homes/` above it at 0700, and its marker.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| NAME | lowercase letters, digits and `-`, a letter or a digit first |
| `--home default` | the default home itself, the same as no `--home` |
| position | before the command; after a command, `--home` belongs to `--host` and names a home of that host |
| refused, exit 2 | when `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME` is also set, when `--home` is given twice, and when NAME is not such a name |
| listing | `dockingbird homes` lists the home by that name from then on |
| seat | a second home on the same computer shares its computer's seat |

heading: The fleet store
summary: The fleet store is one PostgreSQL 18 database, `dockingbird_fleet` by default, that `dockingbird org create` fills.
text: The fleet store is one PostgreSQL 18 database, `dockingbird_fleet` by default, that `dockingbird org create` fills. [The team fleet guide](../../guides/team-fleet.md) installs it.

heading: The fleet store > The three schemas
text:
| Schema | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `fleet` | the fleet scheduler: hosts, workloads, leases, swarm rosters and the workers' samples, with row-level security so a project's role sees its own workloads only |
| `org` | the organisation: its projects, the model and effort of each kind of role, its people and which projects each belongs to |
| `work` | the organisation's work queue, read and written by `dockingbird work` ([the work queue guide](../../guides/work-queue.md)) |

heading: The fleet store > The roles and groups
summary: A name with a dash is written in double quotes in SQL.
text:
| Role | Kind | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `fleet_admin` | login | the admin; makes, grants, revokes and drops the groups itself (it needs `CREATEROLE`); acts for any project; takes no group |
| `fleet_worker_<host>` | login | one machine's worker; a member of `fleet_worker`; its row in `fleet.role_host` names the same host as its `--host` |
| a person's own role | login | one person's commands, their coordinators' and runners'; a member of each project's group they act for |
| `fleet_worker` | group, no login | the workers' rights |
| `fleet_submitter` | group, no login | the submitters' rights |
| `fleet_submitter_<project>` | group, no login | one project; `fleet submit` and `fleet run` take it before they write; `org members add PERSON --project SLUG` makes it when the project has none |

A name with a dash is written in double quotes in SQL. No project has a login of its own. Each login's password is set with psql's `\password`, which sends only the hash, and lives on each computer in a line of `~/.pgpass`, never in a TOML file.

heading: The fleet store > Rules
text:
| Rule | Statement |
|---|---|
| making the store | `org create` makes the three schemas and the groups in one transaction, where the cluster has none, and says `The org store is ready, at version {version}.` |
| a second run | says `The org store is already at version {version}: nothing changed.` |
| who may run it | a role that is a member of `fleet_admin`; any other ends 77 |
| a store from an earlier build | upgraded once after the update by the owner of the `fleet` schema's tables; `org create` as `fleet_admin` applies each missing migration, each in one transaction, when `fleet_admin` owns them |
| another owner | `SELECT DISTINCT tableowner FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname = 'fleet'` names the owner; the [operator guide](../../operator-guide.md) section "The fleet scheduler" gives the command to run as that owner |
| a build that lacks a migration | a worker or admitter refuses to start with `FLEET_STORE_BEHIND` and names the migration; a store that names migrations its build does not know is allowed |
| migration order | the admin's `org create` at the new build runs before any worker or admitter restarts at it; then each machine's worker that runs swarms and the admitter restart; only then use `fleet retire`, `add`, `replace` or `prune` |
| the control plane | its home updates after the admin's `org create` and before the members that joined it |
| a worker that cannot start | it publishes no sample, so after 180 seconds its host is stale and its swarms are interrupted until `org create` migrates the store |
| workers first | move the workers, each publishing one sample at the new build, then the admitter and the submitters; a `fleet submit` at the new build refuses a swarm whose hosts' workers have not published their homes' checkouts |

heading: The fleet store > A store made before the groups were the admin's to grant
summary: Run these as the cluster's superuser, once, for a store whose groups the superuser made.

heading: The fleet store > Older workers
summary: Each row says whether the workers and the admitter of the release before it keep running against a store that migration changed, or restart at the new build first.
text:
Each row says whether the workers and the admitter of the release before it keep running against a store that migration changed, or restart at the new build first.

| Migration | Earlier workers | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `0001_roster_operations` | restart first | adds the roster steps `retire_asked`, `retired`, `pickup` and `held`, which an earlier worker reads as an agent gone and interrupts its swarm; restart every worker and the admitter before `fleet retire`, `add`, `replace` or `prune` |
| `0002_done_after_a_loss` | keep running | adds the state grants of three moves a `done` makes after a loss and changes no move an earlier worker or admitter makes |
| `0003_assignments_told` | keep running | adds `reviewer_told` and `tester_told`, which an earlier worker neither reads nor writes |
| `0004_efficiency` | keep running | its tables, kinds and column are new to earlier builds; move the workers to the new build before the admitter and the submitters |
| `0005_host_rank` | keep running | adds the host rank, null for every host enrolled before it |
| `0006_org` | keep running | earlier workers keep working through it; apply it before any worker, admitter or submitter restarts at the new build |
| `0007_membership` | keep running | as `0006_org`; a project's submitter login keeps working |
| `0008_sql_audit` | keep running | the policies admit the same rows and only plans change; a worker of this build against a store without it refuses to start |
| `0009_rolling_updates` | keep running | adds each process's release, schema, kind and homes and each roster row's release and code; newer records wait until every live process is updated |
| `0010_role_config` | keep running | adds each roster row's `config_digest` and the event kind `denied_by_role`; a worker writes them only once every live process is at this migration |
| `0011_work_queue` | keep running | adds the `work` schema, which no worker or admitter reads or writes, and changes nothing in `fleet` or `org` |

`org create` names the version it reached after each run.

heading: Environment variables
summary: Settings reach Dockingbird through the shell that runs it, and each one is spelled `DOCKINGBIRD_` followed by its name.
text:
Settings reach Dockingbird through the shell that runs it, and each one is spelled `DOCKINGBIRD_` followed by its name.
Dockingbird hands every exported setting to the containers that read it, which is why a setting never sits at its default without you knowing.
Only one variable names a folder, `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME`, and one runtime setting, the database statement timeout, is documented by name.

heading: Environment variables > Variables you may set
text:
| Variable | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME` | an absolute path | `~/.local/share/dockingbird` | the folder of one Dockingbird installation, its home; another path gives a second, fully separate installation with its own containers, volumes and image tag |
| `DOCKINGBIRD_DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_S` | a whole number within its bounds | its built-in value | how long one database statement may run, for the check of `connect --database` and for the agents' queries; `export DOCKINGBIRD_DB_QUERY_TIMEOUT_S=60` raises it |
| `DOCKINGBIRD_<NAME>` | a whole number within its bounds | its built-in value | any other runtime setting of Dockingbird: a poll interval, a timeout or a page size; the name is upper case and spelled exactly |

heading: Environment variables > What `DOCKINGBIRD_HOME` refuses
text:
| Value or folder | Result |
|---|---|
| `/`, your home folder, or a folder above it | refused |
| a folder that holds native state (`operator.token`, `mode.json` or `pg`) | refused |
| an existing folder with files in it but no marker | refused; the empty `logs/` that `clean --all` keeps, your `instructions/` and `vaults/` folders, `versions.toml`, `config.toml`, `browser-solver.json`, `hosts.toml`, `fleet.toml` and Finder's `.DS_Store` do not count |
| a path with a space or `%$"'\` in it | not refused, but avoid it: `connect` passes a folder below it to ssh, which cannot take those characters |
| set together with `--home NAME` | exit 2: "--home and DOCKINGBIRD_HOME both name a home; use one of them." |

heading: Environment variables > How a setting behaves
text:
| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| a value outside its bounds, or values that break a rule between settings | the command stops before it runs and names the variable, never its value |
| a name spelled in another case | the command stops before it runs, naming the variable |
| another variable that starts with `DOCKINGBIRD_` and that no command reads | the command stops before it does anything, exit 2, naming the variable |
| a setting of Dockingbird outside Docker (the database's address and roles, the developer's role switch, the host git's path) | the command stops the same way, since Docker mode never uses it |
| a setting changed while Dockingbird runs | the next command says "Dockingbird is running with other settings than this terminal's." and names `dockingbird stop`; the command after that starts Dockingbird with the new settings |
| `dockingbird status` after a change | shows the same lines under "Needs your attention" and restarts nothing |
| who sees a setting | the agents' harnesses read it too, none is a secret, and `docker inspect` shows them |

heading: Environment variables > Variables of other tools that Dockingbird reads
text:
| Variable | Read by | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | the org login | when it is a path from `/`, `org.toml` lives in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dockingbird/`; otherwise in `~/.config/dockingbird/` |
| `PGPASSFILE` | the org login and the fleet commands | names the PostgreSQL password file in place of `~/.pgpass`; it must be yours and readable by you alone |
| `DOCKER_HOST`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT` | every command that uses Docker | name the Docker daemon Dockingbird reaches, as for any docker command; Dockingbird otherwise uses the current context |
| `UV_INDEX_ZEUSFYI_USERNAME`, `UV_INDEX_ZEUSFYI_PASSWORD` | uv, at install | the index's user name (`license`) and your license key as its password; the key reaches uv in its environment only |
| `SHELL` | `dockingbird completion --install` | picks the shell whose completion script is written, unless you name one |

heading: Limits
summary: This page lists the bounds the Dockingbird guide gives a figure for, one row for each bound.
text:
This page lists the bounds the Dockingbird guide gives a figure for, one row for each bound.
A row holds the figure, what it limits and the page that explains it.
Where a config or a flag changes a bound, the row says which one, and a bound without a figure in the guide has no row.

heading: Limits > Agents and sessions
text:
| Bound | Figure | What it limits | Explained in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session of a bus agent | 12 hours by default, 1 to 168 | how long an agent runs before it ends itself; set with `--session-hours` or `[limits] session_hours` | [app-config.md](files/app-config.md) |
| Turn deadline | none | a turn runs until it ends, unless a config sets `[limits] turn_minutes` (at least 1) | [app-config.md](files/app-config.md) |
| Idle stop | 30 minutes | Dockingbird turns itself off after this long with no agent; the next command turns it back on | [daily-loop.md](../guides/daily-loop.md) |
| Agent numbers | 9999 per tool or command | past it a start without `--as` starts nothing and exits 1 | [delegating-tasks.md](../guides/delegating-tasks.md) |
| Container limits | none unless set | `--cpus`, `--memory` and `[limits] cpus` and `memory` set them | [commands.md](commands.md) |
| Sign-in retries | 3 | a Claude turn that Anthropic refused for its sign-in is tried again after 30, 60 and 120 seconds | [sign-in-and-api-keys.md](../guides/sign-in-and-api-keys.md) |
| Rule retries in a row | 3 by default, 1 to 100 | the retries of one delivery under a `[fallback]` rule; set with `retry_max` | [app-config.md](files/app-config.md#keys-of-fallback) |
| Wait before a rule retry | 5 minutes by default, 1 second to 24 hours | set with `[fallback]` `retry_wait` | [app-config.md](files/app-config.md#keys-of-fallback) |
| Usage-limit retries | after 1, 5 and 15 minutes, then every 30 minutes, until 24 hours after the first failure | a `usage_limit` failure under a `[fallback]` rule; `retry_wait` and `retry_max` do not apply | [app-config.md](files/app-config.md#keys-of-fallback) |
| Moves to the fallback tool | 1 per agent by default | an agent never moves back and forth between its tools | [your-own-commands.md](../guides/your-own-commands.md#a-fallback-tool) |
| Fallback pick-ups | 3 per agent | the pick-ups the fallback watcher on this computer runs for an agent before `status` names the command | [your-own-commands.md](../guides/your-own-commands.md#a-fallback-tool) |
| `fleet probe` | 20 seconds per read, 60 seconds in all | a read of this Mac and its Docker | [hosts.md](../guides/hosts.md) |

heading: Limits > Files and sizes
text:
| Bound | Figure | What it limits | Explained in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rules text of one agent | 64 KB | Dockingbird's rules plus the project's rules file; a longer text stops the start | [trust-and-repo-settings.md](../guides/trust-and-repo-settings.md) |
| `--agent-md` and `--claude-md` file | 1 MB | a regular UTF-8 text file with no Dockingbird credential in it, else nothing starts | [commands.md](commands.md) |
| Entries of one `skills.path` or `--skills` | 16 | the skill folders or skills folders one config's `[skills]` or one `--skills` names | [skills.md](../guides/skills.md) |
| Skills of one agent | 32 | a config's and a start's together | [skills.md](../guides/skills.md) |
| Files of one skill | 64 | the files under one skill folder | [skills.md](../guides/skills.md) |
| Depth of a skill's file | 8 path parts | how deep a file may sit under its skill folder | [skills.md](../guides/skills.md) |
| One skill file | 1 MiB | one file of a skill | [skills.md](../guides/skills.md) |
| One agent's skills | 4 MiB | all its skills together, as Dockingbird records them | [skills.md](../guides/skills.md) |
| Codex's skills listing | 10,000 tokens | the `skills.max_context_tokens` Dockingbird sets for a Codex agent with skills | [skills.md](../guides/skills.md) |
| `hosts.toml` | 1 MiB | a regular file of yours; a larger one is refused | [hosts-file.md](files/hosts-file.md) |
| Host name | 56 characters | lowercase letters, digits and dashes, one per file, never `local` | [hosts-file.md](files/hosts-file.md) |
| Service program output | 64 MiB and 10,000 entries | what a program you connected as a service may write to its output folder | [connections.md](../guides/connections.md) |
| First image build | about 1 GB, about 5 minutes | the download of the first `dockingbird claude`, once | [first-run.md](../getting-started/first-run.md) |
| Ubuntu package pool | 441 MB | the folder the first build fills, once per snapshot | [first-run.md](../getting-started/first-run.md) |

heading: Limits > Swarm definitions
text:
| Bound | Figure | What it limits | Explained in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Definition file | 64 KiB | one `swarm.toml` | [swarm-definition.md](files/swarm-definition.md) |
| Brief or instructions file | 1 MiB | one text a role names | [swarm-definition.md](files/swarm-definition.md) |
| Parameters | 32 | the entries of one definition's `[params]` | [swarm-definition.md](files/swarm-definition.md#parameters) |
| Parameter name | 32 characters | letters, digits and `-` | [swarm-definition.md](files/swarm-definition.md#parameters) |
| `text` parameter value | 120 characters, or the parameter's `max_chars` | one printable line | [swarm-definition.md](files/swarm-definition.md#parameters) |
| Agents of a swarm at its start | 24 | the roles' counts together, and each role's `count` and `max` | [swarm-definition.md](files/swarm-definition.md#role-keys) |
| Helpers at once | 20 | a role's subagent `max` | [roles-and-connections.md](files/roles-and-connections.md#subagent-block) |

heading: Limits > License
text:
| Bound | Figure | What it limits | Explained in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Computers per seat | 3 | one seat is one person with up to three computers; a second home on one computer shares its computer | [licensing.md](../guides/licensing.md) |
| Activations list | 80 computers | `license activations` shows the 80 seen longest ago and says how many more there are | [licensing.md](../guides/licensing.md) |
| Unreleased computer | 90 days | a computer never released stops counting by itself after this long | [licensing.md](../guides/licensing.md) |
| Check-in | once a day | a start whose last check-in is older checks in first; a failed check-in never stops the start | [licensing.md](../guides/licensing.md) |

heading: Limits > Fleet and control plane
text:
| Bound | Figure | What it limits | Explained in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Computer label | 8 characters | lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter, in `cp token --host LABEL` | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Agent name on a joined home | 63 characters less the label and its dash | a longer name is refused with `FLEET_NAME_TOO_LONG` | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Control plane overview | 100 fleet sessions | `status` on the control plane and `cp status` list this many and say `truncated` past it | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Join bundle | 4096 bytes | what `node join` decodes | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Fleet call | 30 seconds | how long a call waits for its answer | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Agent's fleet inbox | 10 seconds | a read or heartbeat from an agent's own fleet inbox | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Silent control plane | 40 seconds | a member finds a silent control plane within this time, then reconnects by itself | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Messages waiting for one fleet agent | 200 | messages to a fleet agent whose home is asleep, held on the control plane's store | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Hub connections | 1024 | one for each member and one for the control plane | [team-fleet.md](../guides/team-fleet.md) |
| Store connection | 5 seconds | how long each fleet scheduler command waits for the database; then it ends 69 | [exit-codes.md](integration/exit-codes.md) |
| `fleet run` wait | 30 minutes by default | `--wait`; a lease not taken by then is given up and the command ends 1 | [fleet-scheduler.md](../guides/fleet-scheduler.md) |
| `fleet run` bound | at most one day | `--bound`; at the bound the command is interrupted and `fleet run` ends 124 | [fleet-scheduler.md](../guides/fleet-scheduler.md) |
| `fleet read-home` | 200 agents and rows, 30 seconds per home | the rest is counted | [hosts.md](../guides/hosts.md) |
| ssh to a host | 15 seconds | a host that does not answer in this time is not reached | [hosts.md](../guides/hosts.md) |

heading: Limits > Tools and tool calls
text:
| Bound | Figure | What it limits | Explained in |
|---|---|---|---|
| First tool download | 15 minutes | how long a start waits for a first download of Claude Code or Codex, or for a version you pinned | [updates.md](../guides/updates.md) |
| `agent_wait` | 1 to 45 seconds | the `timeout_s` of the MCP tool | [mcp.md](integration/mcp.md) |
| Docker waking | 2 minutes | how long a command waits for Docker to answer after a sleep, then it says Docker is answering slowly | [daily-loop.md](../guides/daily-loop.md) |

heading: Ports and hosts
summary: This page lists each port and route Dockingbird opens or expects, the interface it is on, and the hosts an egress mode reaches.
text: This page lists each port and route Dockingbird opens or expects, the interface it is on, and the hosts an egress mode reaches. [Networking](../guides/networking.md) explains the three routes.

heading: Ports and hosts > Ports the control plane and the agents open
text:
| Port or route | Interface | Opened by | Reached by | Guide |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TCP 4222 (`NATS_PORT`), the fleet hub | published by Docker on the control plane computer's loopback only | `cp init` | member computers, once you serve the port to your private network | [Tailscale](../guides/tailscale.md) |
| TCP 9464 (`METRICS_PORT`), `/metrics` of one agent | inside that agent's container network; no port of the computer reaches it | the agent's container | nothing outside the container; `fleet scrape` prints the same lines | [metrics](../guides/metrics.md) |
| `FLEET_SCHED_METRICS_PORT`, the admitter's `/metrics` | the org pointer's database host | `fleet admitter` | your Prometheus | [metrics](../guides/metrics.md) |
| ssh to a host | the host's ssh port, as your own ssh configuration reaches it | your own ssh | `fleet hosts set --ssh`, `fleet agents`, `fleet attach` | [hosts](../guides/hosts.md) |
| `gcloud compute ssh` to a VM | whatever your gcloud uses; with no external IP it uses IAP TCP tunneling | your own gcloud | `fleet hosts set --gcloud` | [other networks](../guides/other-networks.md) |
| the fleet database, PostgreSQL | the `host` and `port` of `org.toml` | your PostgreSQL | every fleet scheduler command, each host's worker, the admitter | [team fleet](../guides/team-fleet.md) |

heading: Ports and hosts > Timeouts and sizes of the routes
text:
| Bound | Value | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| `FLEET_SSH_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S` | 15 s | the ssh connect of a host read |
| `FLEET_PROBE_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_S` | 20 s | each read of `fleet agents --host` and `fleet probe` |
| `FLEET_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S` | 60 s | a whole `fleet probe` |
| `FLEET_HOME_READ_TIMEOUT_S` | 30 s | each read of `fleet read-home` and `fleet scrape` |
| `FLEET_DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S` | 5 s | a fleet scheduler command's connection to the fleet database; a failure ends 69 |
| `NATS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S` | 30 s | a fleet call's wait for its answer |
| `AGENT_PERIODIC_RPC_TIMEOUT_S` | 10 s | an agent's own fleet inbox read and heartbeat |
| `NATS_PING_INTERVAL_S`, `NATS_PING_MAX` | 40 s in all | a member finds a silent control plane, then reconnects by itself |
| `NATS_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | 1024 | connections to the hub: one per member and one for the control plane |
| `NODE_BUNDLE_MAX_BYTES` | 4096 bytes | a bundle, decoded |
| `ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES` | 1048576 bytes | a fleet attachment |
| `HOST_LABEL_MAX_CHARS` | 8 | a computer's label in the fleet |

heading: Ports and hosts > What an egress mode reaches
text:
| Mode | Reaches |
|---|---|
| `full` | every host, from the agent's own network with NAT out and no proxy; the default |
| `allowlist` | its tool's own hosts (the model API and the sign-in), the hosts of its presets, and the hosts of its config's `allow`, through a proxy container, on every port of an admitted host |
| `models` | its tool's own hosts alone |
| `none` | nothing; no network at all, the model API included |

heading: Ports and hosts > Hosts of the presets
text:
| Preset | Hosts |
|---|---|
| `github` | `github.com`, `api.github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `*.githubusercontent.com` |
| `registries` | the package registries of the ecosystems GitHub's recommended allowlist names: npm and Yarn, PyPI, crates.io, the Go module proxy and checksum database, RubyGems, Maven Central and the Gradle plugin portal, NuGet, Packagist and pub.dev, and Hex |

heading: Ports and hosts > Entries of allow
text:
| Entry of `allow` | Reaches |
|---|---|
| `docs.python.org` | that host, on every port |
| `*.corp.example` | every name under that domain |
| `registries` or `github` | the hosts of the preset |
| an internationalized name (an `xn--` label) | refused when the config is read |

heading: Ports and hosts > What the proxy answers
text:
| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `407` | the host is not in the list, or its address is not public, or the request names an upstream proxy of its own |
| `502`, `504`, `500` | the host is in the list, and its name does not resolve or it does not answer |

heading: Ports and hosts > Addresses the proxy refuses
text:
| Address | Answer, listed or not |
|---|---|
| the computer, your LAN, `host.docker.internal`, Docker's own ranges, another agent's address | `407` |

heading: Ports and hosts > Docker version
text:
| Needs | Value |
|---|---|
| a proxy mode (`models`, `allowlist`) | Docker Engine 28 or later |

heading: Ports and hosts > Hosts the computer itself reaches
text:
| Host | For |
|---|---|
| `license.zeus.fyi` over HTTPS | installing and updating Dockingbird from the release index |
| the pinned public base images' registries | the first build of Dockingbird's image, pulled without your login; Dockingbird pushes nothing |

heading: Ports and hosts > When it fails
summary: - [`FLEET_HOSTS_NOT_REACHED`](../troubleshooting.md#fleet_hosts_not_reached): a host route did not answer.
text:
- [`FLEET_HOSTS_NOT_REACHED`](../troubleshooting.md#fleet_hosts_not_reached): a host route did not answer.
- [`NATS_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE`](../troubleshooting.md#nats_server_unavailable): the hub did not answer.
- [`EGRESS_PROXY_FAILED`](../troubleshooting.md#egress_proxy_failed): the proxy of a `models` or `allowlist` start did not come up.
- [`START_NETWORK_POOLS_FULL`](../troubleshooting.md#start_network_pools_full): Docker has no address range left.

heading: Metrics reference
summary: This page is generated from the release's own `fleet scrape` and `fleet queue --metrics` output, and the names and types printed there are the authority.
text: This page is generated from the release's own `fleet scrape` and `fleet queue --metrics` output, and the names and types printed there are the authority. [The observability page](../concepts/observability.md) explains the sources. The Help column of each row is the release's own `# HELP` line. The Meaning column is a short gloss. In the exporter's table, the Help column names the probe field each series is read from.

heading: Metrics reference > Agent families
summary: Every family has the prefix `dockingbird_agent_`, the type gauge, and the labels `profile`, `agent`, `session` and `tool`, plus `team` and `role` for an agent of a swarm.
text:
Every family has the prefix `dockingbird_agent_`, the type gauge, and the labels `profile`, `agent`, `session` and `tool`, plus `team` and `role` for an agent of a swarm. `dockingbird fleet scrape` prints them and each agent's container serves them. The Extra labels column lists what a family adds.

| Family | Type | Extra labels | Unit | Help | Meaning |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `dockingbird_agent_info` | gauge | `model`, `effort`, `state` | from the release's output | from the release's output | the agent's model, effort and state as labels |

| `dockingbird_agent_turns` | gauge | none | turns | from the release's output | turns finished since the process or thread started |

| `dockingbird_agent_turn_running` | gauge | none | 0 or 1 | from the release's output | a turn is running |

| `dockingbird_agent_last_turn` | gauge | `state` | from the release's output | from the release's output | the last turn, its state as a label |

| `dockingbird_agent_last_turn_timestamp_seconds` | gauge | none | seconds | from the release's output | Unix time the last turn ended |

| `dockingbird_agent_context_used_tokens` | gauge | none | tokens | from the release's output | context in use |

| `dockingbird_agent_context_window_tokens` | gauge | none | tokens | from the release's output | the model's context window |

| `dockingbird_agent_compact_at_tokens` | gauge | none | tokens | from the release's output | the context size at which the agent compacts |

| `dockingbird_agent_compactions` | gauge | none | count | from the release's output | compactions since the process or thread started |

| `dockingbird_agent_changed_paths` | gauge | none | paths | from the release's output | changed paths in the agent's copy |

| `dockingbird_agent_untracked_paths` | gauge | none | paths | from the release's output | untracked paths in the agent's copy |

| `dockingbird_agent_changing` | gauge | none | from the release's output | from the release's output | the agent's copy is changing |

| `dockingbird_agent_screen_held` | gauge | none | 0 or 1 | from the release's output | the agent's screen is held |

| `dockingbird_agent_sign_in_retry` | gauge | none | count | from the release's output | sign-in retries |

| `dockingbird_agent_token_failed` | gauge | none | 0 or 1 | from the release's output | the agent's token failed |

heading: Metrics reference > Agent families
summary: Model tokens and costs count from the start of an agent's process (Claude) or thread (Codex) and fall to zero when it restarts.
text:
| `dockingbird_agent_bus_losses` | gauge | none | count | from the release's output | connections to the bus lost |

| `dockingbird_agent_api_retries` | gauge | none | count | from the release's output | API retry events, Claude only |

| `dockingbird_agent_model_tokens` | gauge | `model`, `type` | tokens | from the release's output | tokens per model, type is input, output, cache_read or cache_creation |

| `dockingbird_agent_model_cost_usd` | gauge | `model` | US dollars | from the release's output | cost per model, Claude only |

| `dockingbird_agent_result_input_tokens` | gauge | none | tokens | from the release's output | input tokens of the last result |

| `dockingbird_agent_result_output_tokens` | gauge | none | tokens | from the release's output | output tokens of the last result |

| `dockingbird_agent_result_cache_read_tokens` | gauge | none | tokens | from the release's output | cache read tokens of the last result |

| `dockingbird_agent_result_cache_creation_tokens` | gauge | none | tokens | from the release's output | cache creation tokens of the last result |

| `dockingbird_agent_result_reasoning_output_tokens` | gauge | none | tokens | from the release's output | reasoning output tokens of the last result, Codex only |

| `dockingbird_agent_result_cost_usd` | gauge | none | US dollars | from the release's output | cost of the last result, Claude only |

| `dockingbird_agent_result_duration_seconds` | gauge | none | seconds | from the release's output | duration of the last result |

| `dockingbird_agent_result_turns` | gauge | none | count | from the release's output | turns of the last result |

Model tokens and costs count from the start of an agent's process (Claude) or thread (Codex) and fall to zero when it restarts. Take `delta()` or `deriv()` of them. A Codex agent has no cost and no `api_retries`, and its per-model tokens and compactions stay empty until its rollout has been read.

heading: Metrics reference > Fleet families
summary: The admitter serves these on its own port, and `dockingbird fleet queue --metrics` prints them.
text:
The admitter serves these on its own port, and `dockingbird fleet queue --metrics` prints them. A family may carry more labels than listed. Use `rate()` or `increase()` on the counters only.

| Family | Type | Labels | Unit | Help | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fleet_queue_depth` | gauge | `priority` | workloads | from the release's output | workloads in the queue, by priority |
| `fleet_reserved_millicores` | gauge | `host` | millicores | from the release's output | CPU reserved on the host |
| `fleet_reserved_mib` | gauge | `host` | MiB | from the release's output | memory reserved on the host |
| `fleet_headroom_millicores` | gauge | `host` | millicores | from the release's output | CPU left to reserve on the host |
| `fleet_headroom_mib` | gauge | `host` | MiB | from the release's output | memory left to reserve on the host |
| `fleet_gate_red` | gauge | `host` | count | from the release's output | red gate lines of the host |
| `fleet_host_stale` | gauge | `host` | 0 or 1 | from the release's output | the host's sample is stale |
| `fleet_interrupted` | gauge | `host` | workloads | from the release's output | interrupted workloads on the host |
| `fleet_holds` | gauge | `reason` | workloads | from the release's output | held workloads, by reason |
| `fleet_agent_cap` | gauge | `host` | agents | from the release's output | the host's agent cap against its fullest home |
| `fleet_admissions_total` | counter | `host` | count | from the release's output | workloads the host admitted |
| `fleet_starts_total` | counter | `host` | count | from the release's output | agent starts on the host |
| `fleet_queue_wait_seconds_total` | counter | `host` | seconds | from the release's output | seconds workloads waited before the host admitted them |
| `fleet_agent_seconds_total` | counter | `role`, `host` | seconds | from the release's output | agent seconds of the role on the host |
| `fleet_agent_idle_seconds_total` | counter | `role`, `host` | seconds | from the release's output | idle agent seconds of the role on the host |

heading: Metrics reference > The exporter's gauges
summary: These come from the [example exporter](../../examples/observability/exporter.py), not from the release.
text:
These come from the [example exporter](../../examples/observability/exporter.py), not from the release. They sit on the same page as the agent families.

summary: On each agent line the exporter adds a `home` label.
text: On each agent line the exporter adds a `home` label. The `host` label is not the exporter's: your Prometheus attaches it from the job's `labels`, as [prometheus.yml](../../examples/observability/prometheus.yml) shows.

heading: Fleet tools
summary: An agent whose tools include `bus_send`, started on a home that joined a control plane, gets these ten tools beside its bus tools.
text: An agent whose tools include `bus_send`, started on a home that joined a control plane, gets these ten tools beside its bus tools. [The control plane concept page](../concepts/control-plane.md) explains the fleet, and [the team fleet guide](../guides/team-fleet.md) joins a computer.

heading: Fleet tools > The ten tools
summary: The harness shows each tool's arguments with the tool.
text:
| Tool | What it does | Reach |
|---|---|---|
| `fleet_send` | sends a message; a `question` sent to the operator is listed by `dockingbird questions` on the control plane's home and answered there with `dockingbird answer ROW` | a fleet agent by its fleet name, an agent of the control plane's home by its name, or, with no `to`, `parent`, the operator on the control plane's home |
| `fleet_inbox` | lists the deliveries of the agent's fleet inbox, which sits beside its own inbox | the agent's own fleet inbox |
| `fleet_read` | reads one delivery | the agent's own fleet inbox |
| `fleet_ack` | acknowledges a delivery | the agent's own fleet inbox |
| `fleet_wait` | waits for a delivery | the agent's own fleet inbox |
| `fleet_thread` | works with a fleet thread | the agent's own fleet session |
| `fleet_withdraw` | withdraws a message | the agent's own fleet session |
| `fleet_artifact_put` | puts an attachment, at most 1,048,576 bytes, that a message can name | the agent's own fleet session |
| `fleet_artifact_get` | gets an attachment a message names | the agent's own fleet session |
| `fleet_whoami` | tells the agent who it is in the fleet | the agent's own fleet session |

The harness shows each tool's arguments with the tool.

heading: Fleet tools > Names and inboxes
text:
| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| fleet name | the computer's label, a dash and the agent's name, such as `lab-notes-1` |
| label | one to eight lowercase letters or digits, starting with a letter |
| name length | at most 63 characters less the label and its dash, else `FLEET_NAME_TOO_LONG` |
| two inboxes | the agent reads its own inbox and its fleet inbox, the more urgent delivery first |
| a choice or a plan to approve | asked on the control plane first, and on the agent's own home when the control plane does not take it |
| no answer at the start | the agent starts and works on its home, with `FLEET_SESSION_NOT_OPENED`, and gets its fleet inbox once the control plane answers |
| status line | `fleet: <label>-<name>, heartbeat <age>, asks <n>`, `fleet: not open` or `fleet: none` under each running agent in `dockingbird status` |

heading: Fleet tools > Limits
text:
| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| a fleet call's wait for its answer | 30 seconds |
| an agent's own fleet inbox read or heartbeat | 10 seconds |
| deliveries waiting for one agent whose home is asleep or offline | at most 200 |
| a fleet attachment | at most 1,048,576 bytes |
| fleet calls while the control plane is silent | refused at once, until the member reconnects within 40 seconds |

heading: Fleet tools > What does not cross
text:
| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| a home's work, runs, claims and publication | stay on the home |
| a fleet thread and a home thread | two threads; a message sent on one store is never seen on the other |
| the home's own `questions` list | shows none of the fleet's questions |

heading: Search the docs
summary: `search/search.py` searches every page of these docs on your own computer.
text: `search/search.py` searches every page of these docs on your own computer. It reads two files from the `search/` folder and needs no network or package.

heading: Search the docs > Before you start
summary: - `python3 --version` must print 3.9 or a later version.
text:
- `python3 --version` must print 3.9 or a later version.
- Run the command from the root of a clone of this repository, where the `search/` folder is.

heading: Search the docs > Search from a clone
summary: Open the page at the anchor to read the whole section.
text:
```bash
python3 search/search.py "trust" --top 1
```

```text
1. docs/guides/trust-and-repo-settings.md#1-mark-a-checkout-untrusted  score 55.21
   Trust and repo settings > 1. Mark a checkout untrusted
   dockingbird trust --off
```

| Line | What it shows |
|---|---|
| 1 | the rank, the page with the section's anchor, the score, and `(phrase)` when the section holds the whole query |
| 2 | the heading path, from the page title down to the section |
| 3 | the section's first line, cut at 160 characters |

Open the page at the anchor to read the whole section. Flags work as queries too, so `python3 search/search.py --json` lists every section that uses `--json`.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--top N` | prints N sections instead of 10 |
| `--audience NAME` | doubles the score of sections for one reader: `first-day`, `daily`, `integrator` or `team-admin` |
| `--index PATH` | reads another `index.json.gz`, with its `chunks.jsonl` in the same folder |

| Exit status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | at least one section matched |
| 1 | no section matched, and the command printed `no results` |
| 2 | an option is wrong or an index file is missing, and the message names it |

heading: Search the docs > The files the build writes
summary: A workflow runs `.github/scripts/build_index.py` on every push to `main` and commits what it writes.
text:
A workflow runs `.github/scripts/build_index.py` on every push to `main` and commits what it writes.
A rebuild overwrites these files, so change the pages and leave the files to the build.

| File | What it holds | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| [llms.txt](../llms.txt) | one line per page with its summary, in reading order, under Start here, Concepts, Guides and the rest | a coding agent on its first read |
| [docs/manifest.json](manifest.json) | one record per page: path, title, summary, audience, the commands it shows and the message ids it names | a script or an agent that picks pages by audience, command or id |
| `search/index.json.gz` | the word counts of each section, field by field | `search/search.py` |
| `search/chunks.jsonl` | one line per section: page, heading path, anchor, text, commands, flags, ids, tool names, audience, first sentence | `search/search.py`, and any tool that wants the text |
| `docs/troubleshooting/<area>.md` | ten index pages, each message id of one area with the line saying when it appears | a reader who knows the area but not the id |
| `search/search.py` | the search command, copied from `.github/scripts/` | you |

The build exits 1 and the workflow commits nothing when a page breaks a rule.
It checks for missing front matter, links to missing files, unclosed code fences and ids the catalogue lacks.
The file `search/queries.txt` pairs 30 queries with the page each one must find.
The workflow fails when one of those pages drops out of its query's top 3.

heading: Search the docs > How the search ranks
text:
1. A word the docs never use becomes the closest word they do use, at most two letters off. The output prints each correction on its own line, above the results.
2. A section that holds a query of three or more words, word for word, comes first. A line copied from the screen therefore lands on its message's entry.
3. A message id, an MCP tool name, and a command or flag shown in a `bash` block score five times a plain word. A word in a heading scores twice a word in the text.
4. A flag keeps its dashes and a tool name keeps its underscores, so each stays one word. Ids also split at `_`, so `completion already` finds `COMPLETION_ALREADY`.
5. A command counts by its subcommand, so `trust` finds every section whose `bash` block runs `dockingbird trust`.
6. When the query names a message id, that id's entry in the [catalogue](troubleshooting.md) ranks above every guide. Words that spell an id with spaces count as naming it. Otherwise the guides and the other pages rank above the catalogue.
7. With `--audience`, sections written for that reader score twice as high as the rest.
8. Equal scores follow the reading order of `manifest.json`, from getting started to reference.

A long section cut into several parts appears once in the results, at its best part.

summary: This page is the long reference for running Dockingbird, one section per topic.
